The Deal Notebook in Fusion Loan IQ (hereinafter referred to as Loan IQ) allows the user to add a new or update an existing Origination or Distribution Primary (syndicate member), or, if deal has been approved, allows lender share changes and allows an Origination Primary or an approved Distribution Primary to be closed.

Adding a new syndicate member (via 'Create Primary" screen) or selecting an existing member for update opens up the Circle Notebook. Since a syndicate may be set up with only member names, without specifying any dollar amounts and/or percentages, the user may exit directly back to the Deal Notebook (returning to the Primary List page). However, before the syndicated deal can be closed, the deal must have facilities, each member's share of the syndicate must be established and, if Host Bank is the Admin Agent, the total of all closed origination primaries and closed distribution primaries must add up to the global amount of the syndicated deal.

Body.notes:
Beginning with Release 6.0.10.05 (Patch), the following applies as per the separately licensed enhancement, Transaction Cost Calculation and Amortization:
In the event that there is an Assignment Buy, Participation Buy, Participation Buy More or Subparticipation Buy, a transaction cost is adjusted based on the change to the facility portfolio share amount. Specifically, for every portfolio allocation, the transaction cost is adjusted.
When transaction cost is based on 'Commitment Amount', the amount of the adjustment is calculated as follows:
The amount change to the facility portfolio share amount * Current Transaction Rate
The effective date of the Transaction Cost is equal to the settlement date (Circle Close Date) of the Circle Buy.
If the transaction cost is based on the 'Funded Amount', the transaction cost is adjusted for each portfolio share in each outstanding with non-zero funding decision. The amount of the adjustment is calculated as follows:
The outstanding portfolio share amount * Current Transaction Rate
In the event of a circle Sell Back, the adjustment of the transaction cost resulting from the associated buy circle will be reversed as of the settlement date of the sellback transaction.

First page of circle notebook appears if a circle is selected from the list. items.label: text
items.orig: Note on RIDS: Loan IQ uses the following mechanism to generate RIDs, which are unique not only to a particular table but also throughout the database. The RID field is an 8-byte character string, which logically is split into two sets - a prefix and suffix. The RID is constructed such that it generates discreet character sets, which will uniquely identify a Loan IQ entity (deal, facility, customer, etc.) The RID prefix is the first two bytes of the character set and are randomly generated from a predefined character set. The last six bytes, the RID suffix, represent the number seconds elapsed since 1993-01-01-00.00.00.00, and are represented as a 6-byte base 36 value in character format. If multiple RIDs are generated in 1 second, 1 additional second is added to the previous RID value.

Required (for circle approval) if Percent of Deal is not entered. If amount is entered, corresponding percent of global deal will be calculated by the system. (If desired, percent of global deal can be entered and amount will be derived.) Primary - Indicates lender's amount of the deal. Circle Sell: Indicates total amount across all facilities in the deal to be sold to lender. Circle Buy: Indicates total amount across all facilities in the deal to be sold by lender. Notes : The aggregate amount of the circle is always expressed in the currency of the deal. The facility amounts of the circle are always expressed in the currency of the facility. Multicurrency has been added to circle, to the extent that the aggregate deal level amounts are now calculated and validated using the appropriate FX rates when aggregate is entered. Individual Lender Shares of the Facility Commitment are in the Currency of the individual facility. System uses facility F/X rate, which for 'In' Currencies is the spot Rate from the Euro Funding Desk. i.e. conversion is through the Euro. 'Out' Currencies use the spot rate from the Funding Desk of the facility branch, or the user entered F/X rate from the facility.

Required (for circle approval) if amount is not entered. If percentage is entered, corresponding amount will be calculated by the system. Percentage entered cannot be greater than 100% . Note: The deal/facility fx rate is frozen at circle close. Thereafter, if the facility fx rate changes, it does not affect the circle (the aggregate amount of the circle is still based on the old fx rate). Therefore, when the system calculates the percent of the global at the deal level, it is using the aggregate circle amount at the old rate.

Body.overview:
Beginning with Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch), the Cash on Transfer functionality is available for separately licensed clients. A Cash on Transfer indicator has been added to the Facilities tab to enable or disable the Cash on Transfer functionality for a trade. When the Cash on Transfer indicator is checked for a trade, this indicates that the user cannot select any of the remittance instructions set up for a customer in the customer notebook. Instead the user may only select the 'Custom Instructions' available. The user is also unable to release the cashflows involved before closing a Circle when the Cash on Transfer indicator is enabled.
For separately licensed clients with the Enhanced Tax Withholding functionality, a Correction Trade indicator has been added to the Facilities tab. When the Correction Trade indicator is checked, this indicates that the Circle is a correction trade. (For example, to reverse any Lender Tax Withholding applied as a result of the Circle Event Fee, users must check the Correction Trade indicator so the tax withholding amount is treated as the reversal tax amount for the Circle.)
Beginning with Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch) and Release 6.0.09.11, a Trade Correction RID is available only for clients who are licensed for Enhanced Tax Withholding functionality and available when the Trade Correction indicator is set to Y (checked). The field allows entry of a valid Loan IQ circle RID. If the value entered is not a valid circle RID, an error message is displayed. Note: Any RID can be entered, including the RID of the Circle.
Beginning with Release 6.0, the Trade ID is displayed on the title bar of the Circle Notebook.
Beginning with Release 6.0.09.08 (Patch), the title bar of the Circle Notebook displays <Deal Branch Code>/<Deal Name> for clients who are licensed for Highlight Deal Branch functionality.
As per the Expense and Branch Code Association enhancement, available with Release 6.0.08.08, the following separately licensed enhancement applies:
The Expense and Branch Code selection depends on whether the cashflow is from the buyer or seller side. If the cashflow is from the buyer, the Expense and Branch Code is the buyers. If it is from the seller, the Expense and Branch Code is the sellers.
Beginning with Release 6.0.09.02 and forward, Loan IQ automatically calculates and displays the appropriate amount in the Discount box, calculated as: Facility Circle Current Amount x (100% - Buy/Sell Price %) , at the time the Buy/Sell price is entered in the Circle notebook, if the Circle is created via the Circle icon.

Available as a patch to Release 6.0.08.08 (patch) as per the Circle Funding Indicator Default enhancement, system parameter DCSN (Default Circle to Settle Net) determines the default value. 'Settle Gross,' meaning monies owed to Buyer (for fees, discount, etc.) will be paid separately from monies owed to Seller. Remittance Instructions to the Buyer are required when settling gross at a price other than par. 'Settle Net,' meaning fees and discount owed to Buyer will be netted against gross proceeds of sale, and Seller will be paid the difference. If system parameter MCCYD is set to MAINT for the Branch of the Deal, the checkbox on the circle defaults to checked and is protected. Note: A value is not automatically assigned to the 'Settle Discount in Currency of Outstandings' indicator in pending Circles that exist for clients licensed with this functionality. For Licensed clients opening a pending Circle in INQUIRY mode, Loan IQ displays the default setting for 'Settle Discount in Currency of Outstandings' indicator, if it's current setting is NIL , but the Circle will not be updated. For licensed clients opening a pending Circle in UPDATE mode, Loan IQ displays the default settling for 'Settle Discount in Currency of Outstandings' indicator, if it's current setting is NIL . Licensed clients must refer to the Online Help > Portfolio Position > Multi-Currency Discount Analysis for more information. Available in Release 6.0.09.02 and forward, Settling Multicurrency Discount in L/C Currency is an add-on to Multicurrency Discount Analysis. This functionality allows the ability to stipulate whether the discount associated with the Letter of Credit balance is settled in the currency of the L/C or in the currency of the facility. To support this ability, a new branch- specific system parameter is introduced. When set to Yes , SMDLC ( Settle MultiCCY Discount in the CCY of the L/C ) ensures that the discount for the L/C balance is settled in the currency of the L/C. The default value for this parameter is No . All trade settlement cashflows related to the discount are settled as follows: If the MCCYD system parameter is set to Off , all cashflows for the discount are settled in the currency of the facility. If MCCYD is set to Settl (and is not overridden in the individual circle) or is set to Maint , then: That portion of the discount attributable to the funded outstandings is settled in the currencies of those outstandings. If SMDLC is set to Y , that portion of discount attributable to the unfunded L/Cs is settled in the currencies of those L/Cs. If SMDLC is set to N , that portion of discount attributable to the unfunded L/Cs is settled in the currency of the facility. The remainder of the discount is settled in the currency of the facility. To use Settling Multicurrency Discount in L/C Currency, clients must be licensed for Multicurrency Discount Analysis. For more information, please see Loan IQ How to Prepare for 2008 User

All Other Circles: Brings up a window asking user to choose from either 'Lenders in Deal' (default) or All Customers. Choosing 'Lenders in Deal' presents a pick list that also includes pending lenders in the deal and choosing 'All Customers' allows users to select any Customer known to Loan IQ, even ones without Lender Profiles.
Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Buyer

Defaults to "Yes.' All unclosed circles (pending, awaiting approval, approved, awaiting settlement approved, approved for settlement) are adjusted automatically by the system for all decreases (scheduled and unscheduled), but not for any increases. When the circle allocations are reduced, the associated P&L and discount are adjusted accordingly. The "benefit" of the commitment reduction defaults to the Holder of Risk, the Buyer, unless prior to the commitment reduction, the "Benefit of Commitment Reduction" Indicator in the Circle Notebook is changed to indicate the benefit must accrue to the Seller. If the benefit is to the Buyer, an additional portfolio allocation is created for the circle in order to adjust realized P&L. Changing the circle indicator after the commitment reduction occurs does nothing to change the P&L. Note: Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Buyer is no longer being calculated for internal circles. Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Buyer

Defaults to "Yes.' All unclosed circles (pending, awaiting approval, approved, awaiting settlement approved, approved for settlement) are adjusted automatically by the system for all decreases (scheduled and unscheduled), but not for any increases. When the circle allocations are reduced, the associated P&L and discount are adjusted accordingly. The "benefit" of the commitment reduction defaults to the Holder of Risk, the Buyer, unless prior to the commitment reduction, the "Benefit of Commitment Reduction" Indicator in the Circle Notebook is changed to indicate the benefit must accrue to the Seller. If the benefit is to the Buyer, an additional portfolio allocation is created for the circle in order to adjust realized P&L. Changing the circle indicator after the commitment reduction occurs does nothing to change the P&L. Note: Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Buyer is no longer being calculated for internal circles. Note: If benefit of commitment reduction for a sell is negative (because buy/sell price is greater than par), benefit is posted as a receivable instead of a payable. Specifically:

In new circles , the "Distressed" indicator will default to "Y" (checked), if the logged-on user creating the circle belongs to a distressed sales group. In all other cases, it will default to "N" (unchecked), indicating a "Par" circle. The indicator is modifiable by any user with authority to update the Circle. If "Distressed Trade" indicator is set to "Yes", the circle's Target Close Date will be calculated by the system (and protected) as Circle / Trade Date plus the number of business days defined in the "Distressed Settlement # of Days" parameter. Otherwise ("Distressed Trade" indicator is set to "No" or nil), the circle's Target Close Date will be calculated by the system (and protected) as Circle / Trade Date plus the number of business days defined in the "Par Settlement # of Days" parameter. The Target Close Date will be re-calculated (as above) whenever the Circle / Trade Date changes. The default settings for the Interest/Fee Settlement indicators will be based upon the Circle's "Distressed Trade" indicator: If set to "Yes" (distressed), the Interest/Fee Settlement indicators will be defaulted. If the DTSPA System Parameter is set to 'Yes', the users in distressed sales groups may not approve the same circles they sent to approval, and all distressed circles must be approved by users other than the users who sent them to approval. Note: A user assigned to a Distressed Sales Group may not approve a circle (whether or not it is distressed) which that user has sent to approval. However, a user that is not in a Distressed Sales Group may not approve a distressed circle which that user has sent to approval.

Also, no position validation is ever done for Closing Servicing Groups.

items.label: text
items.orig: For the first circle buy (or primary) into a branch, the user must specify an ongoing servicing group for the host bank. When the first buy closes, its host bank ongoing servicing group will be assigned to the branches of its portfolio allocations. [There may be only one branch per facility investment, and each facility investment must reference the same branch. ] However, if a servicing group has already been assigned to a branch but the branch net position is now zero, a circle buy into that branch can change the servicing group assigned to that branch. E.g., servicing group 1 is assigned to branch A, which has a zero net position. A circle buy assigns servicing group 2 to the host bank. Closing the circle buy will cause servicing group 2 to be assigned to branch A.

The third part displays the Remittance Instructions for the Selected Servicing Group.
Note: Remittance Instructions are assigned to a Servicing Group rather than directly to a particular circle, and a Servicing Group may have the same contacts (members) as another Servicing Group (since it may be desired to assign different sets of Remittance Instructions to the two groups). However, the system will not check that the assigned Contacts and/or Remittance Instructions are, in fact, different (since this would be time-consuming and complicated). Therefore, it is possible that multiple Servicing Groups may have the same members (contacts) and the same Remittance Instructions, and the users must be aware of this fact.
The system-assigned Servicing Group Alias is composed of the first and last initials of each member, separated by slashes, may be modified by the user and must be unique within the lender location. The system-assigned Servicing Group Name is composed of the last names of each member, separated by slashes and must also be unique within the Lender Location. Pressing the 'OK' button assigns the selected Lender Servicing Group to the circle.

table_cells.text: User may select a Trade Settlement Type from the drop-down list. The Trade Settlement Standard drop-down list either does not appear or is disabled on the Codes Tab of Primary Circles, Brokered Assignments, Brokered Participations, Internal Trades, Closed Circles. The items available for selection are populated based on those entries defined by the user in the Trade Settlement Number of Days table in Table Maintenance. The Trade Settlement Branch and Portfolio Mapping table in Table Maintenance is used to determine the default value for the Trade Settlement Standard. The value set for the Trade Settlement Standard is initially blank, but when the portfolio allocations are completed, the value of the Trade Settlement Standard defaults as follows: If there is a row (Loan IQ searches the table by the Order column) found on the Trade Settlement Branch and Portfolio Mapping table that matches the Branch of the Circle's Deal, or matches both the Branch of the Circle's Deal and the first Portfolio Code of the Circle, then the value of the corresponding Trade Settlement Standard, as defined on the Trade Settlement Number of Days table will be the default value in the Trade Settlement Standard drop-down list. If there is not a row (Loan IQ searches the table by the Order column) on the Trade Settlement Branch and Portfolio Mapping table that matches the Branch of the Circle's Deal, or both the Branch of the Circle's Deal and the first Portfolio Code of the Circle, then the value of the Trade Settlement Standard will default to blank. The user may change the selection manually. Note the following: The user may manually change the setting of the Trade Settlement Standard at any time and the Target Close Date will be recalculated, provided the circle has been updated. The value of the setting of the Trade Settlement Standard determines the trade settlement number of days that will be used by the system in calculating the Target Close Date (T + X; X being the trade settlement number of days that is defined in the Trade Settlement Number of Days table. If the trade settlement number of days does not exist, then the Target Close Date (T + X) will be calculated based upon the value set for the either the PRSND ( Par Settlement Number of Days ) system parameter (which defaults to 10 ) or the DSSND ( Distressed Settlement Number of Days ) system parameter (which defaults to 20 ), whichever applies. Note : The Trade Settlement Standard, Early Days Trades functionality allows calculation of the circle Target Close Date when the trade date occurs on a date that is less than or up to six business dates after the deal close date. The delayed compensation start date is different for these trades and this enhancement supports the automatic calculation of the Target Close Date for these trades. For Early Days Trades, delayed compensation does not accrue until Deal Effective Date + 14. This is separately licensed functionality If you are a licensed client of the Trade Settlement Standards functionality; Refer to the Loan IQ Trade Settlement Standard Indicator in the Circle Notebook Setup & User Guide for more information.

This is separately licensed functionality. If you are a licensed customer, Refer to the Loan IQ Early Days Trades Setup & User Guide for more information. When checked, indicates the Circle is an Early Days Trade

Licensed clients Refer to the E-Settlement topic in Online Help , and the Loan IQ E-Settlement System Edit & Validation Rules for more information. If you are not licensed and would like further information about ESettlement functionality, please contact your Loan IQ Account Manager.

table_cells.text: Designates whether or not the Circle will be sent to the E- Settlement System. This indicator will default to checked ( Yes ). A Circle is eligible for E-Settlement if all of the following criteria are met: The Loan IQ Customer is linked to an E-Settlement Customer. The Deal is linked to a Deal Closer (via the E-Settlement Mapping View window). The associated Risk Book has the E-Settlement indicator set to Yes (checked). The Circle is an Assignment. As per the Changes to Circle Confirmation Page enhancement, available in 6.0.08.02, the E-Settlement indicator is updateable at all times until the circle has been approved for settlement. It is not protected once the trade is approved. Once the circle is approved for settlement, it is not updateable. If the trade has been sent to the E-Settlement System ( TSI ), and the indicator is unchecked, the Loan IQ trade is disconnected from the trade at the E-Settlement System and there will no longer be any interaction between the E-Settlement System and Loan IQ

As per the Changes to Circle Confirmation Page enhancement, available in 6.0.08.02, the E-Settlement indicator is updateable at all times until the circle has been approved for settlement. It is not protected once the trade is approved. Once the circle is approved for settlement, it is not updateable. If the trade has been sent to the E-Settlement System ( TSI ), and the indicator is unchecked, the Loan IQ trade is disconnected from the trade at the E-Settlement System and there will no longer be any interaction between the E-Settlement System and Loan IQ

table_cells.text: with this trade. It will no longer be considered an 'E-Settlement Trade'. When the E-Settlement indicator is unchecked, the following occurs: A warning is issued, alerting the user that they are about to change the trade from an E-Settlement Circle to a regular circle and asking if they wish to continue. Displays the E-Settlement System to which the Deal is linked. The user may select an active E-Settlement System that has already been set up in the E-Settlement system. Once the Circle is Approved, the trade information is sent to the E-Settlement system table in Table Maintenance. If there is only one active E- Settlement system defined, it will be the default selection. As per the Enhance E-Settlement to work with Multiple providers enhancement, available in Release 5.4.08.04 a default E- Settlement System may be defined in the Risk Book table in Table Maintenance. If a default E-Settlement System has been defined for a particular Risk Book, then the E-Settlement System drop- down list will default to the selected E-Settlement System for all trades in or out of portfolios housed in that Risk Book. This may be overridden by the user. Note: The E-Settlement System drop-down list is only available in the 5.4.08.04 SP; this functionality does not work in later releases. In 6.0.08.02 (Patch) , 6.0.08.08, and later releases, the default for the E-Settlement System drop-down list is based upon the following logic: When the trade is created, Loan IQ first checks the E-Settlement Systems that are mapped for the Deal, Agent and Counterparties and determines the set of possible E-Settlement Systems. Loan IQ looks at the circle and determines whether the trade is Par or Distressed . Loan IQ looks at the circle's Trade Settlement Standard indicator to determine whether it is LSTA or LMA . Using Par/Distressed and LMA/LSTA values of the circle, Loan IQ determines which of the E-Settlement Systems from step 1are still eligible based upon the values from the E-Settlement System Ranking table in Table Maintenance . Loan IQ must determine which system fits the criteria (for example, LMA Par , LMA Distressed , LSTA Par , or LSTA Distressed ) and if more than one E- Settlement System fits the criteria, Loan IQ looks at the ranking to determine which system will be the default E-Settlement System in the Circle Notebook. If only one E-Settlement System fits and its ranking is not 'N/A', then that one will be the default E-Settlement System. If none fit, then the trade cannot be sent for E-Settlement. If more than one E-Settlement System fits, Loan IQ will default the E-Settlement System drop-down list to the one with the best rank value ('1' being the highest). Notes: Until the trade is sent to the E-Settlement service provider, Loan IQ will update the default E-Settlement service provider if any changes are made that can affect the default provider. Once the trade has been sent for E-Settlement, any changes to the circle will not reset the default. Any changes made to the Deal/Customer mapping will not impact the default setting. Only those changes done to the circle that can change the distressed indicator or the trade settlement standard will change

Available in Release 6.0.13.05, Loan IQ now supports ISIN and LOANX for Markit Clear Trade Settlement Incoming messages processing. This enhancement supports ISIN and LOANX (as a MIS Code) in addition to the Facility CUSIP for validating facilities during the processing of Markit Trade Settlement incoming messages. The value of ISIN can be used for additional lookup in the similar way in which CUSIP id is currently used. The CUSIP is checked first and if it is not found then it will look for the ISIN. The value of LOANX can be used for additional lookup in the similar way in which CUSIP id is currently used. The CUSIP is checked first and if it is not found then it will look for the ISIN. If the ISIN is not found, then it looks for the LOANX. There can be any combination of (CUSIP, ISIN, LOANX) on the Facility in Loan IQ and the message from Message Director can contain any combination of (CUSIP, ISIN, LOANX) as well since the schema allows for multiple identifiers.

The E-Settlement System application sends an E-Settlement System Internal ID the first time Loan IQ sends a create E- Settlement Trade message. Loan IQ receives the E-Settlement System ID immediately, and it appears in the E-Settlement TradeID field on the Confirm Tab of the Circle Notebook, provided that the trade has been created successfully in the E-Settlement System application. Loan IQ sends back this E-Settlement System TradeID to the E-Settlement System so that the trades in the E-Settlement System may be found easily. The E-Settlement TradeID is sent in the following scenarios: A new Loan IQ trade creation message for a Loan IQ Parent Trade is created. New Loan IQ trade creation for a Loan IQ child trade (Loan IQ Parent is created and cancelled after a child trade is created. That Loan IQ child trade is sent to the E-Settlement system. A Loan IQ parent trade is successfully sent to the E-Settlement System The E-Settlement System creates child trades (two or more) and sends that data to Loan IQ via a SUBAL message with the E-Settlement System Internal Trade ID's (one ID for each child trade). Loan IQ accepts the SUBAL message, stores the E- Settlement System Internal ID's, creates child trades, and sends the E-Settlement System new Loan IQ Circle RID's/Trade ID and the E-Settlement System Internal ID's. rules_table.Rules: E-Settlement

Designates whether or not the Circle will be sent to the E- Settlement System. This indicator will default to checked ( Yes ). A Circle is eligible for E-Settlement if all of the following criteria are met: The Loan IQ Customer is linked to an E-Settlement Customer. The Deal is linked to a Deal Closer (via the E-Settlement Mapping View window). The associated Risk Book has the E-Settlement indicator set to Yes (checked). The Circle is an Assignment. As per the Changes to Circle Confirmation Page enhancement, available in 6.0.08.02, the E-Settlement indicator is updateable at all times until the circle has been approved for settlement. It is not protected once the trade is approved. Once the circle is approved for settlement, it is not updateable. If the trade has been sent to the E-Settlement System ( TSI ), and the indicator is unchecked, the Loan IQ trade is disconnected from the trade at the E-Settlement System and there will no longer be any interaction between the E-Settlement System and Loan IQ with this trade. It will no longer be considered an 'E-Settlement Trade'. When the E-Settlement indicator is unchecked, the following occurs: A warning is issued, alerting the user that they are about to change the trade from an E-Settlement Circle to a regular circle and asking if they wish to continue. If 'Yes' then the indicator is unchecked and the trade is no longer an E-Settlement trade. An internal notification is sent to a designated group of Loan IQ users [unchecking the E-Settlement indicator is a notifiable event in the Notifications Matrix.] Re-checking the E-Settlement Trade indicator will re-link the circle with the TSI trade provided that a trade exists in TSI with a RID that matched the RID of the circle. A message will be sent, resubmitting the trade to TSI. If the indicator was unchecked when the circle was approved, checking the indicator sends the circle to TSI . Provided that both circles are in the same stage and that no data has been updated on with side, the trades will re-synch. If, however, the E-Settlement Trade has moved to a different status or any pertinent data has been updated in either trade, they will not be in synch and will appear on the Exceptions report. Beginning with Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch) and Release 6.0.10.02 and forward, the following E-Settlement Enhancements functionality applies: Users with update authority are allowed to change the status of the indicator from checked to un-checked and the status of the trade from E-Settlement to non-E-Settlement. Users with inquiry or access denied authority can view the indicator but not change it. Note: This existing functionality is now separate under the E- Settlement Mapping function. Please see the User Profile Application Function Security document for more information. Available in Release TBD and patched to Release 6.0.08.08, the following Markit Clear Trade Settlement Phase 2 functionality applies: Limited E-Settlement functionality is applied to outside assignments for this indicator.

Available in TBD Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch), the following separately licensed Markit Clear Trade Settlement functionality applies: Indicates the current status of the Markit trade. The items available for selection are populated based on those entries defined by the user in the Markit ESettlement Status table in Table Maintenance. Users with update authority are allowed to select statuses. Available in Release TBD and patched to Release 6.0.08.08, the following Markit Clear Trade Settlement Phase 2 functionality applies:

rules_table.Rules.Note: Defaulting for Trade settlem: Displays the E-Settlement System to which the Deal is linked. The user may select an active E-Settlement System that has already been set up in the E-Settlement system. Once the Circle is Approved, the trade information is sent to the E-Settlement system table in Table Maintenance. If there is only one active E- Settlement system defined, it will be the default selection. As per the Enhance E-Settlement to work with Multiple providers enhancement, available in Release 5.4.08.04 a default E- Settlement System may be defined in the Risk Book table in Table Maintenance. If a default E-Settlement System has been defined for a particular Risk Book, then the E-Settlement System drop- down list will default to the selected E-Settlement System for all trades in or out of portfolios housed in that Risk Book. This may be overridden by the user. Note: The E-Settlement System drop-down list is only available in the 5.4.08.04 SP; this functionality does not work in later releases. In 6.0.08.02 (Patch) , 6.0.08.08, and later releases, the default for the E-Settlement System drop-down list is based upon the following logic: When the trade is created, Loan IQ first checks the E-Settlement Systems that are mapped for the Deal, Agent and Counterparties and determines the set of possible E-Settlement Systems. Loan IQ looks at the circle and determines whether the trade is Par or Distressed . Loan IQ looks at the circle's Trade Settlement Standard indicator to determine whether it is LSTA or LMA . Using Par/Distressed and LMA/LSTA values of the circle, Loan IQ determines which of the E-Settlement Systems from step 1are still eligible based upon the values from the E-Settlement System Ranking table in Table Maintenance . Loan IQ must determine which system fits the criteria (for example, LMA Par , LMA Distressed , LSTA Par , or LSTA Distressed ) and if more than one E- Settlement System fits the criteria, Loan IQ looks at the ranking to determine which system will be the default E-Settlement System in the Circle Notebook. If only one E-Settlement System fits and its ranking is not 'N/A', then that one will be the default E-Settlement System. If none fit, then the trade cannot be sent for E-Settlement. If more than one E-Settlement System fits, Loan IQ will default the E-Settlement System drop-down list to the one with the best rank value ('1' being the highest). Notes: Until the trade is sent to the E-Settlement service provider, Loan IQ will update the default E-Settlement service provider if any changes are made that can affect the default provider. Once the trade has been sent for E-Settlement, any changes to the circle will not reset the default. Any changes made to the Deal/Customer mapping will not impact the default setting. Only those changes done to the circle that can change the distressed indicator or the trade settlement standard will change The default E-Settlement System cannot default until after the portfolio allocations are completed and saved, unless the user manually selects it. Once Loan IQ has selected the E-Settlement System default, if the user selects another E-Settlement provider, and chooses to send the trade, Loan IQ will only validate whether the selected provider is mapped to a Deal and Customer. Available in Release 7.2.4 and Release 6.0.13.05 the following Markit Clear Trade Settlement Phase 2 functionality applies: Limited E-Settlement functionality is applied to outside assignments for this indicator. Note: Defaulting for Trade settlement standard is supported for outside assignments via the API/Front-End and if the value is passed via the API it overrides the table default. Available in Release 6.0.13.05, Loan IQ now supports ISIN and LOANX for Markit Clear Trade Settlement Incoming messages processing. This enhancement supports ISIN and LOANX (as a MIS Code) in addition to the Facility CUSIP for validating facilities during the processing of Markit Trade Settlement incoming messages. The value of ISIN can be used for additional lookup in the similar way in which CUSIP id is currently used. The CUSIP is checked first and if it is not found then it will look for the ISIN. The value of LOANX can be used for additional lookup in the similar way in which CUSIP id is currently used. The CUSIP is checked first and if it is not found then it will look for the ISIN. If the ISIN is not found, then it looks for the LOANX. There can be any combination of (CUSIP, ISIN, LOANX) on the Facility in Loan IQ and the message from Message Director can contain any combination of (CUSIP, ISIN, LOANX) as well since the schema allows for multiple identifiers.

Loan IQ no longer accept values from the E-Settlement System for this attribute - it is only updateable via the Circle Notebook. The value for the Assignment Fee Decision is included on the mismatch reason for the Exception Reports so that if there is a mismatch in the Assignment Fee Decisions value between a trade in Loan IQ and a trade in the E-Settlement System, then this will appear on the Exception Report. Mismatch reasons are the following: Counterparty (CTPY), Amount (AMT), Trade Date (TRDT), Price (PRICE), Assignment Fee Decisions (AFD). The E-Settlement System application sends an E-Settlement System Internal ID the first time Loan IQ sends a create E- Settlement Trade message. Loan IQ receives the E-Settlement System ID immediately, and it appears in the E-Settlement TradeID field on the Confirm Tab of the Circle Notebook, provided that the trade has been created successfully in the E-Settlement System application. Loan IQ sends back this E-Settlement System TradeID to the E-Settlement System so that the trades in the E-Settlement System may be found easily. The E-Settlement TradeID is sent in the following scenarios: A new Loan IQ trade creation message for a Loan IQ Parent Trade is created. New Loan IQ trade creation for a Loan IQ child trade (Loan IQ Parent is created and cancelled after a child trade is created. That Loan IQ child trade is sent to the E-Settlement system. A Loan IQ parent trade is successfully sent to the E-Settlement System The E-Settlement System creates child trades (two or more) and sends that data to Loan IQ via a SUBAL message with the E-Settlement System Internal Trade ID's (one ID for each child trade). Loan IQ accepts the SUBAL message, stores the E- Settlement System Internal ID's, creates child trades, and sends the E-Settlement System new Loan IQ Circle RID's/Trade ID and the E-Settlement System Internal ID's. items.label: list_item
items.orig: 1. "Circled' Option is available to Circles in "Pending" or "Awaiting approval" status that have not been circled already. It sets the "Circled" Amount to the Current Amount and sets the Circled/Legal Trade Date , but does not change the circle status . Circled/Legal Trade Date must be a valid business day, cannot be greater than today, and defaults to the current date (or to the previous business day, if today is not a business day), but may be changed at any time, by anyone with circling authority, to reflect a different effective date (either when the event is created, or subsequently by drilling down on the event and entering another valid date). Changing the Circled/Legal Trade effective date will appear as an individual event.

Verify Buy/Sell Price
When the Circle Notebook is initialized for an existing circle, all information is "display only.' Choosing the "Update" Option switches the user from "Inquiry Mode" to "Update Mode,' locking the record and allowing the user to modify/update selected circle information, as applicable. All other Options on the Option pulldown menu that update the circle and that are available to the user are now unprotected and may be selected. Only users who are authorized to update the circle in its present state may choose the 'Update' Option. Three possibilities exist : "Update Pending Only,' Update Open Only' and "Update Closed Only.'
I nformational message is issued if user attempts to open the Circle Notebook in Update Mode while the Facility Notebook is open. Message indicated that the Circle Notebook can only be opened in Inquiry Mode (since the Facility Notebook is open).
Error message is issued if user attempts to switch an open Circle Notebook from Inquiry into Update Mode while the Facility Notebook is open.
Putting a circle into Update Mode locks only time regions of the facilities affected by the circle. In addition, whenever portfolio allocations are created or updated, the time regions of the facilities affected by the circle are locked.
This Option is always available to switch the user out of "Update Mode,' and returns the Circle to "display only.'
Certain Items must be noted in the templates for the LMA letters:
Note: Beginning with Release 5.5 and forward, the following functionality applies. Both Addressee and Addressor emails are included on the Header of both the LSTA/LMA confirmation letters.
Note: Although the sample-distressed template indicates a percent calculated as utilized/facility commitment, it has been determined that this is not necessary; the drawn (i.e., funded) amount by facility is sufficient.
The Generate Confirmation Letter option is available only to external non-pooled Host Bank Assignments and Participations that have already been circled.
The confirmation maybe created manually or automatically, depending on the Trade Confirms settings made in the LS2APP.INI file. If the Auto Merge Documents indicator is set to Yes , in the LS2APP.INI File (Trade Confirms), then selecting the Generate Confirmation Letter option brings up the Create Trade Confirm window.
Body.notes:
If the Auto Merge Documents indicator is set to No, in the LS2APP.INI File (Trade Confirms), then the confirmation letter must be generated manually. Refer to the Quick Reference Card LSTA&LMA Confirmation Letter Quick Reference Card , available on the Loan IQ Support Site (under the Business Trade Confirms link) for information on creating confirmation letters manually.
The Confirmation Letter Received option cannot be selected unless the circle has a Buy/Sell amount greater than zero. Receipt of the Confirmation Letter will circle an Origination Primary that has not already been circled. No other circle Option affects the Confirmation Letter Received information. Receipt of Confirmation Letter is not required to close a circle, and is not allowed unless Circle Buy/Sell amount is greater than zero.
Note: As per the Enhance Zero Value Trades enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05 (Patch also for 08.02), the following functionality applies:
Loan IQ now allows Confirmation Received events to be generated for Zero Value trades.
The Confirmation Letter Received event may be recorded at any time (even after a circle is closed). It will default to the current date, but may be changed at any time to reflect an earlier effective date (either when the event is created, or subsequently by drilling down on the event and entering another valid date). Effective Date is validated against Holiday Calendars associated with branch of the deal. A Warning is issued if Effective Date is a non-business day. Changing the Confirmation Letter Received effective date will appear as an individual event.
When a Confirmation Letter is marked as received in the Circle Notebook, the Confirmation Letter Document in Doc Tracking, if there is one, is also marked as received (if it has not already been so marked). Conversely, marking a Confirmation Letter Document as received in Doc Tracking updates the Circle's Confirmation Letter Received information.
Confirmation Letter generated by circle includes a deal level total discount amount paid to the buyer, which is calculated properly (using the correct FX Rate) for circles in multi-currency deals.
If the Trade Confirmation Letter Received date is before the circled legal/ trade date ( Trade date ), then the warning message 'The trade confirmation date<> is earlier than circled /Legal trade date<> '. Do you wish to continue?' appears. User can choose Yes to continue.
If the Circled/Legal trade date is updated in such way that the updated date is after Confirmation Letter Received date , then the warning message 'The circled /Legal trade date<> is later than trade confirmation date<>. Do you wish to continue?' appears. User can choose Yes to continue.
If the trade Confirmation Letter Received Date is after the Expected Close Date , then the warning message 'Trade confirmation received letter date<> is later to Trade Close date. Do you wish to continue?' appears. User can choose Yes to continue.
If the Expected Close Date is updated in such a way that the date is prior to Confirmation Letter Received Date , then the warning message ' Expected closing date<> is earlier than Trade Confirmation letter received date<>. Ignore error and continue?' appears. User can choose Yes to continue.

Selection of this option sends the trade to the E-Settlement system manually and can be selected multiple times as long as the circle has not been sent to settlement approval for both circle buys and sells. When this menu is manually selected Loan IQ creates an event and a trigger.
Note: Event Management has to be setup to initiate the appropriate (Inception or Update) message to the E-Settlement system. For more information, licensed users may refer to the Event Management help on creating events and triggers. Non-licensed users interested in learning more about this functionality must contact their Loan IQ Account Manager for more information.
All mandatory fields must be entered in a trade before it can be sent to Markit. Any changes to the mandatory fields after a trade inception is successfully sent to Markit, triggers the trade amendment message.
The list of Events and corresponding messages that get triggered are:
All trade messages must be processed in sequence.
The initial trade is automatically sent to Markit upon approval of the circle if all criteria are met. Criteria are as follows:
Event Management checks these validations upon approval of a trade. If one of the criteria is not entered/setup properly, event management stops processing the trade and an error message 'Trade inception message cannot be sent to Markit <Buyer MEI is missing>' is displayed.
Loan IQ sends the trade inception message to Markit when trade is sent to Markit. If the trade inception message is not sent to Markit, none of the other trade messages are sent. After the trade is resent to Markit, Loan IQ resends the trade inception message to Markit. Once a trade inception message is sent to Markit successfully, Loan IQ only sends the 'Trade Amendment' messages to Markit thereafter.
After a trade is successfully sent to Markit, the E-Settlement status of the trade displays 'Pending' on the confirm page of the circle notebook.
After a trade is matched in Markit, Markit sends a trade match message to Loan IQ. The e-settlement status of the trade is changed to 'Matched' on the confirm page of the circle notebook.
New event 'Trade is matched' and 'Confirmation letter received' are created in Loan IQ. Drilling down to this event retrieves the exact trade messages Loan IQ receives from Markit.
After the trade is matched in Markit, the Markit trade identifier is populated in the E-settlement TradeID field on the confirm page in the circle notebook. Markit trade Identifier is displayed in the trade match event comment. The Markit Trade Id is 15-25 characters, alphanumeric. Example of the Markit Trade Id is MC0000000000000012.
After a trade is sub-allocated, the E-Settlement status for all child trades displays 'Matched' on the confirm page of the circle notebook.
After a trade is matched, if Loan IQ amends the trade, Loan IQ sends the trade amendment message to Markit. If the other counterparty amends the trade, Markit sends a trade status update notification message to Loan IQ. The E-Settlement status is changed to 'Suspended' on the confirm page in the circle notebook.
New event 'trade is suspended' is created. Drilling down to this event retrieves the exact trade messages Markit sends to Loan IQ.
Trade is allowed to be removed at the parent trade level or at the individual child trade level.
A trade is considered 'Removed' when the trade is changed to non-Markit from Markit trade.
After users change the E-Settlement system in Loan IQ, Loan IQ sends a trade remove message to Markit. The E-Settlement status changes to 'Blank' on the confirm page in the circle notebook.
An event 'E-settlement system is changed' and 'Trade is removed' is recorded. Drilling down to this event retrieves the exact trade messages Loan IQ sends to Markit.
Once the trade is removed in Loan IQ, all other trade messages are ignored from the Markit thereafter.
If a trade is removed from Markit and assigned to Clear Par, Loan IQ triggers the trade remove message and automatically resends the trade to Clear Par and vice versa. However, if a trade is changed from Markit to E-Settlement other than Clear Par, the user has to manually resend the trade to the selected ESettlement system.
Cancellation message will be triggered at the master level only.
After a trade is cancelled in Loan IQ, Loan IQ sends the trade cancellation message to Markit. The ESettlement status of the trade is changed to 'Cancelled' on the confirm page in the circle notebook.
Once the trade is cancelled in Loan IQ, all other trade messages are ignored from the Markit thereafter.
If the trade is sub allocated, after the last child trade is cancelled, Loan IQ sends the trade cancellation message to Markit with the parent trade Id.
If one of the child trades is cancelled, it generates an amendment at the parent level for the remaining amount.
Sub allocation can be created in Loan IQ or by Markit. If sub allocation is created in Loan IQ, Loan IQ does not send any trade message to Markit. The link between Loan IQ and Markit will be broken. If suballocation is created in Markit, Markit sends the trade allocations message to Loan IQ. Loan IQ creates the child trades via trade API based on the allocations message.
If a trade is amended in Loan IQ, Loan IQ sends the trade amendment message to Markit. If a trade is amended in Markit, Markit sends a trade status update notification to Loan IQ. The E-Settlement status of the trade is changed to 'Suspended' or 'Matched' based on the Markit message on the confirm page of the circle notebook.
All trade amendment messages are triggered at the master level.
If a trade is sub-allocated and users modify the trade amount, trade price, trade type, trade settlement type, other terms of trade or trade date at an individual child trade in Loan IQ, a warning message is displayed:
'Warning: The trade is price is changed at one child trade; all other child trades must be updated. Do you want to continue? Yes or No'.
If the user clicks Yes to the warning message, Loan IQ sends a trade amendment message to Markit. Markit sends a trade status update notification to Loan IQ. The E-Settlement status of each child trade is changed to 'Suspended' or 'Matched' based on the Markit message on the confirm page in the circle notebook.
After a trade inception is successfully sent to Markit, any changes to the fields Markit used to match trades triggers the trade amendment message.
When users change the customer MEI or facility CUSIP, an event is created on the respective notebook and this event triggers the same trade amend message. Note: Loan IQ writes a new Inquiry API function to get all the Markit trades that are not in closed, cancelled status for the customer or facility then sends trade amend message for each trade.
Users have the ability to view all the failed trades with e-settlement Markit Clear via E-Settlement window Maintenance tab, to use the Retry functionality via E-Settlement screen to resend a failed trade to Markit, and to view all open trades with e-settlement Markit Clear via E-Settlement window - Open Trade tab.
Note: Loan IQ has a hierarchy model to specify the E-Settlement system. Loan IQ uses the E-Settlement system table ranking to determine which E-Settlement system a trade is designated for. Each bank is responsible for adding Markit Clear to the E-Settlement system table and designating what ranking Markit Clear has as an E-Settlement system. Licensed clients Refer to the Circle, E-Settlement, Setup, Table Maintenance help for more information. If you are not licensed and would like further information about ESettlement functionality, please contact your Loan IQ Account Manager.
Available in Release TBD and patched to Release 6.0.08.08, the following Markit Clear Trade Settlement Phase 2 functionality applies.
The Settlement Details message is sent to each counterparty by Markit, after a trade is matched in Markit. Settlement Details messages are sent only to counterparties in the trade but not to Agent. This enhancement provides Loan IQ the ability to process the Settlement Details message sent from Markit.
The Settlement Details message contains key pieces of information such as the delayed compensation calculations, scheduled to close date, revised commitment amount, payment amount, remittance instructions and assignment fees.
The message is processed on trades which are approved and are in open status. If the trade status is not approved, Loan IQ does not process the Settlement Details message and fails the message. After successful processing of the message, Loan IQ sets the trade status to Awaiting close.
The Settlement Details message is not processed if there are any exceptions during the validations and while performing trade workflow steps and will sit in an exception queue for manual processing.
If any validations or workflow steps fail, the state of the trade rolls back to its original state (prior to processing the message).
Users can retry the failed message for processing.
An Event 'Settlement details message' is written in the trade after processing the trade settlement message on the trade. Each incoming Markit trade settlement message is available to view from the event in the trade. Event comments show the overridden values.
Any value which is overridable in Loan IQ by the values in the settlement details message are configurable. Clients have the choice to whether they want to allow the overrides or fail the message if values do not match.
Loan IQ validates attributes of the settlement message against the trade in Loan IQ before processing in Loan IQ. Some values of Loan IQ are allowed for override by the values which are available in settlement details.

Available with Release 7.2.7 with the Markit Phase 2.1 enhancement, Loan IQ captures the Markit Clear Delayed Compensation Amount at the Cost of Carry and Interest/Fee Level and makes adjustments in Loan IQ at the level of Cost of Carry and Interest/Fee level to match the Markit Clear Delayed Compensation. Cost of Carry is included in the Delayed Compensation calculation as a separate line item and makes adjustments based on the Cost of Carry in Loan IQ versus what is transmitted from Markit Clear. Cost of Carry is displayed in the Delayed Compensation.

items.label: text
items.orig: Loan IQ captures the details of the Markit DC calculation sent in the message and displays this information in the delayed compensation module screen for users to compare the difference of the DC calculation components. items.orig: Selection of this Option presents the user with a pop-up dialog allowing the user to create and send a freeform message to any person who has an Active or Notifications Only (Beginning with Release 5.5 and forward) Loan IQ User Profile. Initially, the "Send to" list (Notification List) is populated from the list of Deal Personnel assigned to the deal augmented by the list of salespersons and traders. The user may customize the Notification List before sending the message. The lists of salespersons and traders and personnel assigned to the deal are not changed; only the Notification List is modified, and only for this particular notification. If "Send Notifications" is subsequently selected again for this same circle, the Notification List will initially default again as explained above, and may be customized again. However, the customized version is not saved. The subject box is automatically filled in with the deal and lender names, but may be overridden.

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 1. The Approve for Settlement' function ensures that the cashflows and all accounting entries are correct. When Host Bank is Agent, all circles must be approved for settlement prior to being closed except for the sole lender primary in sole lender deals. When Host Bank is not Agent, the non-host bank primaries are exempted from the 'Approve for Settlement' requirement, but all other circles must be approved for settlement prior to close.

Body.overview:
Loan IQ captures the details of the Markit DC calculation sent in the message and displays this information in the delayed compensation module screen for users to compare the difference of the DC calculation components. The details captured in the DC module from the message are contract, buyer share, days, rate, basis, FX rate, carry rate, delayed comp and accrual. Every time a settlement details message is processed, Loan IQ looks for delayed compensation values in the message (if any) and overrides the Markit delayed compensation values to reflect the new values.
Available in Release 7.2.7 with Markit Phase 2.1 enhancements, Loan IQ has been enhanced to use default Servicing Groups on trades based on Buyer/Seller Servicing Group logic.
Loan IQ uses multi-sorting based on the below attributes to set the default servicing group on the trade by collecting all servicing groups under complete Locations for Customer Lender Profile. Servicing Groups must be sorted in the order listed below:
The first Servicing Group will be selected from the list after applying multi-sorting on the above attributes.
System parameter CSGLT (Customer Servicing Group Logic on Trades) must be set to Y (Yes).
This enhancement modifies the Inquiry API functionality to include this logic.
Note : A default Servicing Group will not be set on the trade if there are no Servicing Groups under complete Locations and if there are no complete Locations under Customer Lender Profile. A default servicing group will not be set on the trade if there are no complete locations under Customer Lender Profile. Servicing Group will be left blank in these scenarios. For all other scenarios a Servicing Group will be defaulted based on the logic above . **This is important because Servicing Group default logic is required for processing Markit Clear Trade Settlement/ClearPar messages via message director (for example, Settlement details, allocation and close messages).
The Settlement Details message has Remittance instructions details. While processing the Settlement Details message, Loan IQ creates a custom instruction on the trade for the cashflows. If there is no Remittance instructions in the message then Loan IQ looks for the system parameter 'Set the Remittance instructions to status None on Markit clear trade '.If the system parameter is set to No, then Loan IQ uses the default Remittance instructions and if the system parameter is set to Yes, then Loan IQ sets the cashflow status to None.
Loan IQ automatically processes the Trade Close message (for counterparty) coming from Markit. Loan IQ closes the trade based on the trade close message regardless of the trade status.
Trade close message processing adjusts the delayed compensation amount in Loan IQ to match the delayed compensation amount received in the settlement details message from Markit.
Trade close event displays the incoming Markit trade close message in the trade and event comments display the overridden values.
If the trade is in a closed status and the closed message is received then Loan IQ ignores the message for processing. The message is considered successfully processed. Each message contains information about one trade only. The trade is identified by allocation ID first and if not found by ID then the ESettlement ID trade ID is used. Failed trade close messages are viewable from the exception queue and users can retry processing the message again.
Note : Retry action changes the status of the message and places the message in the queue for processing.
Loan IQ validates attributes of the trade close message against the trade in Loan IQ before processing in Loan IQ.
Loan IQ automates all the steps for closing a circle utilizing the Markit Clear messages. Loan IQ processes the Settlement Details message to advance the trade to 'Awaiting close' status and automatically closes the Markit Clear trade when the Markit Clear trade close message (for agent or counterparty) is received.
Allows the user to view the submitted trade via the E-Settlement system's website.
The View E-Settlement System Trade menu option is part of TSI functionality, which is separately licensed. Licensed clients Refer to the Loan IQ TSI Link Setup Guide, the Loan IQ TSI Link User Guide, and the Loan IQ TSI Link Edit & Validation Rules for more information. If you are not licensed and would like further information about TSI functionality, please contact your Loan IQ Account Manager.

Selection of this Option presents the user with a pop-up dialog allowing the user to create and send a freeform message to any person who has an Active or Notifications Only (Beginning with Release 5.5 and forward) Loan IQ User Profile. Initially, the "Send to" list (Notification List) is populated from the list of Deal Personnel assigned to the deal augmented by the list of salespersons and traders. The user may customize the Notification List before sending the message. The lists of salespersons and traders and personnel assigned to the deal are not changed; only the Notification List is modified, and only for this particular notification. If "Send Notifications" is subsequently selected again for this same circle, the Notification List will initially default again as explained above, and may be customized again. However, the customized version is not saved. The subject box is automatically filled in with the deal and lender names, but may be overridden.
This Option must be used to change the amount on any existing circle, prior to close, once an initial circle amount has been entered and saved. It is not available after circle close.
The Option is used to change just the Circled Amount, both the Circled and Current Amounts, or just the Current Amount. User may pro-rate a new aggregate amount, or may enter amounts for selected facilities that must add up to the new aggregate amount. User may enter either the "New Aggregate Amount" or "New Percent of Global,' and the system will calculate the value not entered.
If someone who does not have "approval authority" changes the current amount on an approved circle, the circle status reverts to "Awaiting Approval,' and availability is affected as per availability rules. If changed by someone with approval authority, the same validation rules that were enforced when the original pool allocations were performed will be reapplied. If the circle had 'source' portfolio allocations that had been used, the sale's portfolio allocations will be adjusted accordingly. If an increase occurs and insufficient approved available exists, so that the portfolio allocations cannot be automatically adjusted by the system, the existing portfolio allocations will be deleted. The user may always make any further portfolio allocation adjustments desired.
When Change Share Prior to Close is selected for a Pooled Sale, the edit validations that governed the original pool allocations will be reapplied. A warning is issued if Change Share Prior to Close is selected for a Swap or Buyback transaction.
Changing the share(s) of an unclosed circle to zero no longer changes the Buy/Sell price to zero. (However, it is still invalid to try to change the buy/sell price to anything other than zero, if facility investment share is zero).
The following options are available under this Option:
Not a selectable option unless transaction has already been circled. Changes Circled Amount only as of the Circled/Legal Trade Date. Will not alter the current amount.
This is the only option allowed if transaction has not yet been circled. Changes the Current Amount and, if transaction has been circled, also changes the Circled Amount. Effective date is Circled/Legal Trade Date (if one exists) or the current date and cannot be changed. This is the default selection for unapproved distribution circles.
Not a selectable option unless transaction has already been circled. Changes the Current Amount as of the selected date. Effective date defaults to current date but can be overridden to another earlier date not less than Circled/Legal Trade Date. This is the default selection for approved distribution circles, and any Origination Circles (primaries and outside assignments).
Changing the allocated amount on an approved Buy (or Sale to Qualified Buyer) that affects the trading position will increase (or decrease) the usage, as appropriate.
Share changes adjust Trade Date P&L as appropriate. If the Circle is a Sell and the lender's share of any facility investment is being increased, and the circle has portfolio allocations in a portfolio other than an "In Syndication " portfolio, and that portfolio is amortizing, then the Select Purpose of Circle Commitment Increase window appears, and user must choose either "Error Correction (Original WAC)' or "Top-Up after Commitment Reduction (Current WAC).' The portfolio allocations created for the share change will affect P&L based on the Selected WAC (original or current "Weighted Average Cost").
For internal circles, the WAC must be selected even when the share change is being performed for the Buy, since this also causes the sell to increase.
Pooled primaries with Host Bank pool member allocations (and consequent Host Bank outgoing portfolio allocations) are treated like sells for the purpose of selecting either Original or Current WAC.
Changing share prior to close on a circle with ongoing fee skims will adjust the circle's fee skims, as appropriate. Also, for circles that amend participations agreements that have interest skims, changing share prior to circle close will properly adjust the interest skims attached to the source agreement.
When reducing a primary's share of a facility investment to zero, the facility investment will be deleted from the database if:
The deal is not closed
The facility investment has no portfolio allocations, or its portfolio allocations are allowed to be deleted from the database.
A facility whose facility investments have all been deleted from the database can be subsequently deleted itself.
Changing a primary's share of a facility investment to zero does not create an event. (Since share change events point to facility investments, there can be no share change event in this situation).
If Sales Targets exist for a Host Bank Circle and the Circled Amount is changed via a 'Change Share Prior to Close' or a 'Change Share After Close' request, the following warning message is displayed: 'Changing the host bank circled amount will affect Sales Targets. Review Sales Target information.'
The enhancement to the Change Share Prior to Close Option in Circle Notebook functionality is separately licensed and available in Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch) and Release 6.0.09.08.
The Change Share Prior to Close Option functionality in the Circle Notebook has been enhanced to provide the following:
Upon selecting the Change Share Prior to Close option in the Circle Notebook, the Change Share For <> window opens and the New Amount for each facility is automatically pre-populated with the current amount (i.e., the same amount that is in the Old Amount column).
The ability to be able to amend any price on each facility, all on the Change Share Prior to Close window.
When increasing from zero the amount of a facility which currently has a price of zero, the price will automatically be set to the average price of the existing non-zero facilities.
When the Change Share Prior to Close option is selected, Loan IQ auto populates all New Amounts for each facility to be equal to their corresponding Old Amounts in the Circle Notebook. You may then selectively change one or more of the pre-populated New Amount fields to be a different value as well as amend the price on any Facility item. Highlight and drill down on a Facility and a pop-up window opens, whereby you may enter a New Amount and/or New Price . Loan IQ recalculates New Aggregate Amount and New Percentage of Global when a change is entered in the New Amount fields.
When a facility for which the old amount and old price are zero has the new amount set to non-zero, the system automatically sets the new price for that facility to the average price (based on the old amounts and old prices). That default new price may then be changed. You must press OK on the New Amount and New Price window to save all the changes. The average price is calculated as follows:
Loan IQ takes all non-zero shares and prices in the circle and multiplies the Old Amount by the Price, and accumulates one at a time, and when complete, divides the accumulated result by the accumulated Old Amount fields. When a new Facility is added, the Price is defaulted to the Average Price of the previous items. If we add more than one facility item, the Price will be defaulted to the same price. The Average price, after calculation based on the Current Amount and Price of the Facility shares prior to any changes being made, is not saved; it is always recalculated.
Refer to the Loan IQ Enhanced Change Share Prior to Close Option in Circle Notebook User Guide for more information.

If a circle requires portfolio allocations for only one host vehicle (non-pooled external circles), and that booking vehicle has only one branch, or the circle requires outgoing allocations and only one branch for the deal currently has any portfolio position, then default allocations will be created for that branch as follows, if the following conditions are met:
When the option is selected, default portfolio allocations will be created if possible , as follows :
1. If user's Risk Book has only one portfolio/expense code combination:
Buys - Incoming portfolio allocation is automatically created for this portfolio/expense code combination.
Sells - Outgoing portfolio allocation is automatically created for this portfolio/expense code combination, as long as sufficient position exists to cover the allocation.
If user's Risk Book has more than one portfolio/expense code combination:
Buys - Default allocations cannot be made.
Sells - If the facility is totally allocated to only one portfolio/expense code "bucket,' and this portfolio/expense code combination is included in the user's Risk Book, then an outgoing portfolio allocation can be automatically created for this portfolio/expense code combination, as long as sufficient position exists to cover the allocation.
If a circle requires portfolio allocations for more than one host vehicle (pooled circles with pool allocations for more than one host vehicle pool member and internal assignments and participations) or the one host vehicle has multiple branches, selecting "Default Portfolio Allocations" will bring up a screen from which the user must choose the branch for the portfolio allocations. The user must always choose a branch for at least one host vehicle. However, if there are multiple host vehicles involved, the user may select branches for fewer than all the host vehicles (a warning will be displayed). In the latter case, portfolio allocations will, of course, be created only for the host vehicles for which branches were chosen.
For internal trades, the default allocations will always be created for the sell first (if it has a Risk Book), even if default portfolio allocations are selected from the buy. When saving portfolio allocations created for the sell via the portfolio allocations screen, default allocations will be created for the buy if they do not already exist. Warning message will be issued if the default portfolio allocations cannot be created for the buy, so user will know that they were not done.
Branch Selection List - Appears whenever the Branch for a Portfolio Allocation cannot be defaulted. Summary of conditions under which it appears:
-Or -
For Internal Assignments and Participations, if the Branch Selection list is required to be displayed and default portfolio allocations may be made for both sides of the trade, both Host Bank Vehicles will appear in the list. If only one side of the trade qualifies for default allocations, then only its Host Bank Vehicle will appear in the list.
If the Branch Selection List screen must be displayed (because at least one Host Bank Vehicle in the list does not have a default branch), any Host Bank Vehicle in the list that does have a default branch will have that branch automatically filled in by the system before the list is displayed.
On Internal Trades, the default allocations for the buy are always created in the same branch as the allocations for the sell.
If the conditions for the creation of default portfolio allocations are not met, none will be created, and the user must perform the required allocation.
