If there are 3 approvers for a transaction, once approver 1 gives approval, their details are populated for subsequent approvers to view.
Loan IQ provides the ability to approve all the circles/initial drawdowns/SBLC Issuances under a Deal from the Consolidated Approval screen provided users have the required security and authority. The Initial Drawdowns/SBLC Issuances are those that are Awaiting Approval only or in case of circles (Buys), those that are awaiting settlement approval.
The following options are accessible to users from the ' Status ' menu:
Send to Approval Send to Approval/Approve Approve Send to Approval for Settlement Approve for Settlement Return to Pending Return to Open Close Cancel
Show Settlement Approval Status
Can send a circle to approval without having selected either the "Confirmation Letter Received" or the "Circled" event. However, the "circled" event will be automatically generated at "Send to Approval,' if not already present.
If circle is in 'Ticket Mode' and has not yet been circled, the default 'Circled/Legal Trade Date' will be displayed, and the user may change it prior to continuing with the Send to Approval:
If Expected Close Date is not present, 'Circled/Legal Trade Date' defaults to current business date (date on which circle is being sent to approval).
If Expected Close Date is present, 'Circled/Legal Trade Date' defaults to the earlier of the Expected Close Date and the current business date.
All the normal validation rules for 'Circle/Legal Trade Date' will apply if user chooses to modify the default value.
Cannot send a circle to approval if it has zero amounts or is missing a Pricing Comment. Also, with the exception of all Outside Assignments and Broker Transactions and Primaries where Host Bank is not the agent, all facilities in which the lender is investing must have a non-zero Buy/Sell price. If a pooled sale, "Brought In By" must be present. Unless circle is for an Origination Primary or both the Buyer and the Seller are the Host Bank, at least one contact must have been assigned to the circle.
A buyback or participation transfer sell cannot be sent to approval unless the "source of sale" is specified.
Warnings previously issued at "Send to Approval" if aggregate amount of a Circle Buy exceeds trading lines, baskets or positions are currently being bypassed, and will not be reinstated until Trading Lines have been redesigned.
Warnings will be issued at "Send to Approval" if any of the following conditions apply. (User must either acknowledge the warning or cancel the 'Sent to Approval' request):
Circle Sell: If assignment or participation, warning will be issued if aggregate sell amount exceeds host bank's available for sale or if a facility sell amount exceeds host bank's available for sale in the selected facility. This does not apply for internal circles.
Pooled Sale: If pooled assignment sale, warning will be issued if total Host Bank's share of the pooled sale exceeds host bank's available for sale or if total Host Bank's share of a facility exceeds host bank's available for sale in the selected facility. This does not apply for internal circles.
Send to Approval Notifications When circle status is updated to "Awaiting Approval,' an Internal Notification ('Circle send to Approval') is sent to the Distribution List defined in the Notifications Matrix.
Normally, they will be sent to the "Sales & Trading Manager" of any Sales Group to which the deal is assigned and to the Syndicate Manager for the deal.
Note: Send to Approval and Approve are not required for Host Bank Origination Primaries
Combines the "Send to Approval" and "Approve" functionality into a single option.
Both "Send to Approval" warnings and "Approval" warnings (circle includes share of a matured facility, insufficient available for assignments or participations) will be displayed prior to displaying the Approval screen. Warnings that are issued for both "Send to Approval" and "Approval" will be issued only once when "Send to Approval/Approve" is selected.
"Approval" event is created for the circle; the "Send to Approval" event is suppressed.
If the user cancels from the Approval screen, the circle will be rolled back to "Pending,' and any automatic circling will be undone.
For Internal assignments and participations, "Send to Approval/Approve" will approve the selected circle and will update the "Contra" circle to "Awaiting Approval,' since the two circles must be approved independently of one another. An "Approve" event is created for the selected circle, and a "Send to Approval" event is created for the contra circle.
This option is the ' front office approval ' of the circle. and it is not governed by the Approvals Matrix. The approval requirements defined in the Approval Matrix for circles govern its ' Approval for Settlement ,' not its 'front office' approval.
Circle status must be "Awaiting Approval,' all required data and any conditional data applying to this circle must have been entered. Circle cannot have zero amounts, and if distribution, must have at least one salesperson contact. If buyback or participation transfer sell, the required "Source of Sale" must be present.
Note: Once a circle requiring a "source of sale" has been approved, it cannot be saved unless the "source of sale" exists. The required "source of sale" may be changed at any time prior to circle close, but cannot be deleted, and cannot be changed after circle close.
The " Affects Trading Position " indicator is displayed (defaults to "No" on all Internal Circles, to "Yes" on Buys and "No" on Sells) and may be changed if approver possesses the proper update authority. The Customer's "Qualified Buyer" indicator (for the Lender's Booking Location) flows down to the circle, and if "Yes,' the Circle's "Qualified Buyer" indicator may be modified from "Yes" to "No" (only) . The approver will be unable to set the circle's indicator to "Yes" if the customer's indicator is "No.' Note: When any Buy (or Sell to a Qualified Buyer) is approved, it increases (or decreases) the usage against the trading line or basket, as appropriate, if "Affects Trading Position" indicator is set to "Yes."
Warnings will be issued when the "Approval" Option is selected if any of the following conditions apply. (User must either acknowledge the warning or cancel the "Approval" request):
Circle Buy: W arnings previously issued pertaining to trading lines, baskets or positions are currently being bypassed, as is the creation of the "Violation of Trading Lines" event when the aggregate buy amount of the Circle being approved exceeds trading lines, baskets or positions. In future releases, after Trading Lines have been redesigned and the warnings have been restored, the Distribution Manager will be
notified when the warning is overridden, and if the warning is related to exceeding a trading line , the Credit Officer will also be notified.
Circle Sell: If assignment or participation, warning will be issued if aggregate sell amount exceeds host bank's available for sale or if a facility sell amount exceeds host bank's available for sale in the selected facility. This does not apply to internal circles.
Pooled Sale: If pooled assignment sale, warning will be issued if total Host Bank's share of the pooled sale exceeds host bank's available for sale or if total Host Bank's share of a facility exceeds host bank's available for sale in the selected facility. This does not apply to internal circles.
Upon approval, circle status is updated to "Open,' Final Approval Date is set to current date, and Approval event is created. User may not subsequently select the Approval event to change the date of Final Approval.
If a circle is approved without having been previously circled, the Approval Option also sets the Circled/Legal Trade Date and Amount and creates a Circled event (in addition to the Approval event). The displayed Circled/Legal Trade Date defaults to the Approval Date, but may be modified to reflect an earlier date. If a circle is approved after having been circled, only the Approval event is created.
Origination primaries - Host Bank and Non-Host Bank Origination Primaries will only be circled - they will not need to be approved individually. (All Distribution Primaries (which are always Non-Host-Bank) continue to require approval).
A user application function 'Approve No Longer Available for Sale,' has been added to the user profile. User must have update authority for this function in order to approve the following:
circles, other than internal trades, in deals which are no longer available for sale;
assignments in deals, which are no longer assignable;
participations in deal, which are no longer participate-able.
If user selects 'Approve' or 'Send To Approval/Approve' in a situation where the user does not have the proper update authority, an appropriate error message is displayed. If the deal is not for sale and the user chooses 'Send To Approval/Approve', the user must have both 'Send To Approval/Approve' update authority and 'Approve No Longer Available For Sale' update authority; for 'Approve', only 'Approve No Longer Available For Sale' update authority is needed.
For the fast approval function from the circle selection screen (accessed if only awaiting approval circles are selected and the user has 'Approve' update authority), 'Approve No Longer Available For Sale' authority is checked when the user presses the 'Approve' button for a selected circle.
After the circle has been approved and the status is updated to 'Open', an Internal Notification ('Circle Approved') is sent to the Distribution List defined in the Notifications Matrix.
Note: Beginning with Release 5.4 and 6.0, separately licensed functionality, Circle Approval , provides second approval functionality.
Circle Approval only applies to the front office approval functionality that currently exists in the Circle Notebook and utilizes all of the current functionality available for transactions in the Approvals matrix. Circle Approval applies to all Circle types.
When the appropriate approval rules are met a user may only create the circle and send it to approval. A second user must approve the circle. This also includes circle creation by trade entry.
Note: Send to Settlement Workflow item may not appear in the Circle workflow page if the Admin Agent was changed after the Circle has been created.
Note: As per the Enhance Zero Value Trades enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05 (Patch also for 08.02), the following functionality applies:
A message is displayed if Zero Value circles are sent for settlement approval without prior portfolio allocations. The message states that Portfolio/Expense Codes are required to settle event fees. When the message is clicked the Enter Portfolio/Expense Codes for Event Fees window opens to allow Portfolio/Expense Code selection.
'Not enough pool available' generates an error at circle close, but a warning at settlement approval.
If existing portfolio allocations cannot be closed (due to insufficient closed position), neither a warning nor an error is issued at settlement approval.
Warning is issued if the circle closing date is less than the effective date of any of the facilities in which the circle has a share.
Validation performed at circle close that checks the deal status (to see if it is valid to close the primaries) is not performed at settlement approval.
Note: Separately licensed functionality, Suppress Circle Automatic Return to Pending , allows Loan IQ to prevent automatically circles from returning to a pending status when changes are made to the Deal associated with the respective circle(s). This is controlled by the setting of the system parameter, PCRTP (Prevent Circle Automatic Return to Pending). Users may also create one or many exceptions via the Branch and Risk Return to Pending Exception Table in Table Maintenance, so that circles with a specific Branch and Risk Book combination are not automatically returned to pending. Circles will be returned to a pending status when any of the following conditions exist:
A facility is added to a Deal
A scheduled commitment reduction is released
An unscheduled commitment increase in a closed Deal (via an amendment) is released
The Deal amount is changed on a pending Deal OR
The facility amount on a pending Deal is changed
Note: Circles that have a status of Awaiting Settlement Approval and Approved for Settlement are returned to an open status.
All licensed Customers must Refer to the Loan IQ Automatic Return Circle to Pending - Setup Guide for more information. All other interested clients, please contact your Loan IQ Account Manager for more information.
As stated above (see 'Option: Approve for Settlement') once a circle has been approved for settlement, no updates are allowed other than changes in status ('Return to Open', 'Return to Pending' or 'Close'. Selection of 'Return to Open' resets circle status to 'Open', so that additional changes may be made to the circle.
As per the separately licensed Enhanced Approval Process available in Release 6.0.09.08(Patch), the following functionality applies for Circles when a user returns a Circle to Pending or Open state via the Options menu  'Return to Pending' or 'Return to Open' menu option:
The list of processors, who modified the Circle prior to returning the Circle to Pending or Open state, is not deleted by the system. Instead, these users remain as processors of this Circle and all such processors are not allowed to (i) approve the Circle subsequently if the license for ENH 1417 is turned on and 'Processor May Approve' indicator in the 'Online Approval Rule Editor' screen is set to 'N' for Circle Approval or (ii) settlement approve the Circle subsequently if the 'Processor May Approve' indicator in the 'Online Approval Rule Editor' screen is set to 'N' for Circle Settlement Approval transactions. This applies both when returning the Circle from Open/Awaiting Settlement Approval or Open/Settlement Approved and also when returning the Circle from Awaiting Approval or Open when the license for ENH 1417 is turned on.
The user who returned the Circle to Pending or Open state, regardless of whether the Circle was already approved or approved for settlement and regardless of whether the license for ENH 1417 is turned on, is not added as one of the processors of the Circle and is allowed to (i) approve the Circle subsequently, even though license for ENH 1417 is turned on and the 'Processor May Approve' indicator in the 'Online Approval Rule Editor' screen is set to 'N' for Circle Approval transactions or (ii) settlement approve the Circle subsequently, even though the 'Processor May Approve' indicator in the 'Online Approval Rule Editor' screen is set to 'N' for Circle Settlement Approval transactions, provided this user is not already one of the processors of that Circle.
covered facilities again, since this processing area may have changed. (See 'Circle Processing Area' write-up in Appendix).
Primary: Closing the primary prior to deal close causes the total lender contractual gross in the facility to exceed the global amount of the facility. (Applies only to the primaries that are automatically closed by the system when deal closes).
Circle Sell: Host Bank Booking Vehicle net share is insufficient to cover the sale or Host Bank Booking Vehicle gross current is insufficient to cover an assignment sale.
As per the separately licensed enhancement, Income and Expense Deferred to FHAD, available in Release 6.0.10.02, the following functionality applies:
For more details, Refer to the Loan IQ Income and Expense Deferred to FHAD Setup Guide .
Pooled Sale: Cannot close a Pooled Sale if the Deal is not closed. If sale is to a primary, error will be issued if any pool member's share of the sale (aggregate and/or individual facility amount) is greater than member's primary position or greater than his contractual gross amount (whichever is lower) .
If pooled sale is an assignment , error will be issued if any pool member's share of the sale (aggregate and/or  individual  facility  amount)  is  greater  than  member's contractual  gross  amount .  All  pool member positions are checked, and pooled sale cannot close unless all proposed pool allocations can be satisfied.
Validation of pool members' Servicing Group positions will be performed at close (and at "Change Share After Close") to insure that the Non-Host Bank Pool Members' Servicing Group position does not become negative
Circle Buy: Host Bank is admin agent and aggregate buy amount exceeds seller's total commitment amount or facility buy amount exceeds seller's commitment amount in that facility.
Post-Closing Primary: Closing a primary after the Host bank deal has closed is not permitted. NonHost Bank primaries attached to closed Non-Host Bank Deals may still be closed.
All Circles: The Branch assigned to the Servicing Group for a Host Bank must be the same as the Branch of the Host Bank Lender's portfolio allocations.
When the Host Bank is the Agent, Primary and Assignee Servicing Groups are not permitted to have a negative position.
Primary: Warning is displayed when system closes a primary that has a share of a facility that has pending or active outstandings, pointing out that closing the primary will not automatically affect the loan  funding  (since  Primaries  do  not  have  funding  decisions)  and  user  must  adjust  the  funding manually. Warning is not issued when closing non-host primaries in a non-host agent deal (since Loan IQ does not keep track of funding in these cases).
Circle Buy: Warnings previously issued if aggregate buy amount exceeds trading lines, baskets or positions  are  currently  being  bypassed,  and  will  not  be  reinstated  until  Trading  Lines  have  been redesigned.
Circle Sell: Warning that the circle must be closed immediately is issued if portfolio allocations are being made out of an amortizing portfolio.
All Circles: Warning is issued at circle close if an active loan is past its repricing date, and therefore will not be automatically adjusted. Warning is also issued if the circle closing date is less than the effective date of any of the facilities in which the circle has a share. User must acknowledge the warning in order to continue the close process.
Closing a circle that has not yet been "circled" gives the user the option of generating the "circled" event as a by-product of the close. The user may then enter the Circled/Legal Trade Date or allow it to default to the Circle Close Date. Again, Close Date may not be a future date, may not be prior to Circled /Legal Trade date. For assignments and participations, the circle close date cannot be earlier than the Deal Close Date.
Important Note: If the discount rounding adjustment calculated at circle close is greater than the  maximum set on the Currency Table in Table Maintenance, for any one branch and currency, the circle cannot be closed. Error message is issued displaying the amount of the buyer's discount or premium, the total portfolio discount and the total portfolio P/L.
Since the calculation of discount amount for cashflows and funding memo is slightly different from the calculation used for determining its offset for gl entries, there is a possibility that the two amounts
can be slightly different (because of rounding). In Release 5.1, there is a maximum (set by the User) per currency. If the difference is not greater than this maximum, that difference is written to a miscellaneous account. If the difference is greater than the maximum the error is raised.
Important Note : Circle now validates all funding decisions during circle close (rather than discontinuing the validation when the first error is encountered). The complete list of validation errors is then presented to the user and may be kept open while the necessary adjustments are made. If no validation errors are encountered, circle close proceeds to completion.
Note: Transaction cannot be released if a Cashflow Settlement Currency has been chosen, but no F/X Rate has been set. User must set the F/X Rate for the Settlement Currency in order to release the transaction.
Note: Circle close functionality is available to all users attempting to close a circle that has non-book amounts. Clients must set up the appropriate G/L Short Name for Realized P&L - Non Book (the RPNBK G/L Short Name), otherwise they will receive a mapping error. The appropriate mapping must be set up before the circle can be closed.
cancelled circle is deleted, and since sent faxes cannot be deleted, a circle with sent faxes cannot be deleted).
Any  type  of  canceled  circle  may  be  made  a  marketing  circle,  including  internal  assignments  and participations and internal trades, and making one side of an internal circle a marketing circle also makes the other side a marketing circle.
The reason for cancellation of a previously canceled circle can be changed by selecting the Effective Date button (on Circle Events page) when the most recent Cancellation Event is highlighted . The same 'Cancel Circle' screen opens, except the 'GL Entries' button is not shown. If a circle is currently a marketing circle and is currently linked to other circles, the cancellation reason may not be changed until the links are deleted . (The cancellation effective date may also be changed, and a new comment may be added.)
Linked Circles - Any circle that is not inactive (not canceled and not terminated) may be linked to any marketing circle (regardless of circle type). Refer to 'Option: Link/De-Link With Marketing Circle' and 'Option: Show Marketing Links' for more information.
Note: Circle cancellation will generate G/L Entries if there is any Benefit of Commitment Reduction affecting the circle.
Note: As per the Extension of AutoStart Allocation Functionality enhancement, available with Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch), 6.0.09.11 and later releases, the following separately licensed enhancement applies:
Loan IQ provides the ability to automatically make portfolio allocations for the sells short when the user cancels the buy. This prevents the need to manually modify the portfolio allocations of any circle sells against the trade date available for the portfolio allocations of the buy in order to cancel the Buy. Prior to this enhancement, if the circle sells were not modified manually prior to the attempt to cancel, an error was received.
trade date update time stamps due to the following are ignored: allocation changes due to facility commitment reduction, allocation changes to benefit of commitment reduction, allocation changes due to manual benefit of commitment reduction, and any allocation when the amount is zero.
All circle types can cover a short internal trade sell.
This option is available to all non-canceled circles until they have been approved for settlement.
The status screen lists all rows from the Approvals Matrix that apply to the settlement approval of this circle, based on matching by branch, host bank net and total amount of the circle and host bank net outstandings after this circle closes. Rows pertaining to circle's settlement approval are shown regardless of whether this circle would currently generate warnings. For each row, an asterisk is shown next to each approval requirement that has already been met. Screen also displays a list of details for the users who have already approved this circle for settlement, if any.
Drilling down on a row in the list of approved requirements opens the 'Online Approval Detail Viewer' identifying every user who has already approved this circle for settlement. If settlement approvers are required by location, screen lists the affected locations and shows the users from each location that have already approved the circle for settlement. If approvers are not required by location, 'Not Applicable' is shown in the list box.
Note : If approvers by location are required but portfolio allocations have not been entered yet, the circle does not yet have any locations, and 'Not Applicable' will be shown.

items.label: text
items.orig: Loan IQ allows creation of Block Trade Allocations for Zero Value trades. Users can create allocations to other lenders and Loan IQ creates subsequent child trades and permanently cancels the parent circle. When the allocations for the child trades are created, a record of the percentage the allocation was of the original parent trade is created for each child circle, even though the amount of the child circles are zero. This percentage appears in the Event Comment for the create event on the child circle.

items.orig: Portfolio Allocations If the original circle has only one portfolio allocation, that portfolio allocation and all of its attributes (price, marks, discount, etc.) will transfer to the new circles with the amounts being prorated based on the amounts of the new circles. table_cells.text: Percent of Source displays the percentage of the source circle represented by the amount that has been allocated. Brings up the 'Select Lender' window. Will default to the Lender who is the Buyer/Seller of the parent circle. In order for other lenders to appear for selection in this window, a customer must have the Buyer/Seller Customer of the parent circle defined as its Immediate and/or Ultimate Parent in its customer notebook. If no other lenders have the Buyer/Seller of the parent circle defined as the Immediate/Ultimate parent, then the Buyer/Seller of the parent circle will be the only lender to appear for selection. System permits allocation to the Parent lender. Body.overview:
Before selecting any of the Maintenance Options that will update the circle, the Circle Notebook must be in "Update" mode. If necessary, the user must select "Update" from the other Options menu before proceeding.
Available for Assignment and Participations (both Buys and Sells), prior to the circle being sent to Settlement Approval. Not available for Primary Circle, Internal Circles, Internal Trades, Brokered Trades, Outside assignments, Sub Participations, Pooled Circles, etc. Block trade allocations may be created only once the Circle Amount has been entered and the facility commitment amounts have been allocated. Selecting 'Block Trade Allocations' from the Maintenance Menu in the Circle Notebook will bring up the Block Trade Allocations Screen, which will allow the user to allocate the circle amount to other lenders. Upon closing the Block Trade Allocations Screen after the original circle amount has been fully allocated, new circles will automatically be created for each lender and the original 'parent' circle will be permanently cancelled.
The new 'child' circles will inherit the following from the 'parent' circle (if they have been entered): Buy/Sell Price, Portfolio Allocations, Host Bank Buyer or Seller Servicing Group, Pricing Comment, Fee Skims, Portfolio for Fee Skims, Discount, Buy/Sell Calculated Price, Settings for Interest/Fee Settlement Decisions, Interest Skims, Portfolio for Interest Skims, Target Close Date, Expected Close Date, Conditions To Close, MIS Codes, Salesperson/Traders, Affects Trading Position indicator, and comments from the Comments Page (the author of the comments from the Comments Page or Pricing Comments in the new circles will be the User ID of the person who created the Block Trade Allocations). Please note: any fees entered on the Event Fees screen of the Parent Circle will not be carried over to the Child Circles.
Note: As per the Block Trade Enhancement of Event Fee enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05 (Patch also for 08.02), the following separately licensed functionality applies:
The following event fees are populated from the Parent Circle to each of the Child Circles:
Internal commission
Assignment recordation fee/Participation transfer fee
Broker fee
Delay compensation
One time post trade date fee payment
Accrued fees bought and sold
Breakfunding
The event fee amounts on the Parent Circle are populated for each of the Child Circles, pro-rated based on the respective Percentage of Source. The ability is provided to modify the values after the Child Circles are created.
Note: As per the Enhance Zero Value Trades enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05 (Patch also for 08.02), the following functionality applies:
Loan IQ allows creation of Block Trade Allocations for Zero Value trades. Users can create allocations to other lenders and Loan IQ creates subsequent child trades and permanently cancels the parent circle. When the allocations for the child trades are created, a record of the percentage the allocation was of the original parent trade is created for each child circle, even though the amount of the child circles are zero. This percentage appears in the Event Comment for the create event on the child circle.
Delayed compensation accrued for the parent is copied to the child circles pro rata based on the entered amount/percentage for each child circle.
The description of the 'Cancelled' Event on the Events Page of the parent circle will state that the circle was cancelled due to creation of Block Trade Allocations. An Event 'Block Trade Allocation' will be created in the child circles, stating that the circle was created via a Block Trade Allocation. Drilling down on this event will bring the user to the Permanently Cancelled parent circle.
Note: Once a parent circle has been 'Permanently Cancelled' due to the creation of a Block Trade, selecting the 'Block Trade Allocation' option from the Maintenance Menu will bring up a list of all the Pending Circles created by the allocation (similar to the regular 'Select Lender Commitment Screen', except that only pending child circles will appear). Conversely, the pending circles created by the Block Trade Allocation will be visible in the regular Select Lender Commitment Screen
Note: A circle that has been 'Permanently Cancelled' due to the creation of Block Trade Allocations may not be deleted. (Although circles created as a result of Block Trade Allocations may be deleted once they have been cancelled, provided they meet with the regular criteria for deletion of a circle).
Portfolio Allocations If the original circle has only one portfolio allocation, that portfolio allocation and all of its attributes (price, marks, discount, etc.) will transfer to the new circles with the amounts being prorated based on the amounts of the new circles. The WAC must flow down to the Allocation Circles. The WAC for the child circles must therefore be the same as the parent circle.
Similarly, If more than one allocation exists for the original circle, those allocations and all their attributes (price, marks, discount, etc.) must also transfer to the new circles, the amounts being pro-rated based on the new circle amount. The WAC for the child circles must therefore be the same as the parent circle.
Note: Due to rounding differences when the trader discount is calculated on the original circle as opposed to when it is calculated separately for each new, smaller trade allocation circle, it is possible that in some cases the trade discount and weighted average cost will not be exactly the same as when there was only the original circle.
Benefit of Commitment Reduction - If Benefit of Commitment Reduction occurs in the original Parent Circle, whether entered manually in the Parent Circle or as a result of a Facility Commitment Reduction (prior to the creation of the Block Trade Allocation while the Parent Circle was still an open trade), the original amount of the Benefit of Commitment Reduction will be prorated across the child circles. Regardless of how many Benefit of Commitment Reductions have occurred for the original circle, the new
child circles will only have one Benefit of Commitment Reduction (and portfolio allocation per Portfolio Bucket for the Benefit of Commitment Reduction) will appear in each of the child circles and will be done as a Benefit of Commitment Reduction Adjustment in the circle, effective on the business date when the Block Trade Allocation was created. The amount will be an aggregate of each prorated Benefit of Commitment Reduction amount.
The Immediate and Ultimate Parents of the original Counterparty must also appear in the selection list, as long as those parents have completed Lender Locations.
For example, if Customer 'A's Immediate Parent is Customer Y and Customer 'A's Ultimate Parent is Customer Z, then Customer Y and Customer Z must also appear in the selection window when the user chooses to allocate.
Note that in order to distinguish between the lender's aggregate amount and the lender's individual facility amounts, the lender aggregate row appears in blue and the facility rows appear in black.
Body.notes:
Option is available prior to circle close, as long as the circle's Servicing Group has been established. For pooled circles, pool allocations must be performed first (before cashflows can be created). Cashflows are required before circle can be approved. Cashflow screen that appears when the 'Cashflows' option is selected displays the Deal/Facility and Main Branch above a list box displaying all of the Cashflows associated with the circle. The Status, Payment Method, Customer Short Name (prefixed by 'To' or 'From'), Left to match, Transaction Amount, Matched Amount, Currency, Account Number and Name (ABA/DDA Number, etc.), UID, Beneficiary Account, Beneficiary Type, Division, Date Done, Time Done, Expense Code, Priority, and Servicing Group Name, SG Alias, SG Location and Watchful Account Indicator are displayed for every cashflow, as applicable, and user can drill down to view/change the cashflow details.
So that the user need not scroll back and forth to see important cashflow information, a Browser has displays the following fields from the selected cashflow item: Servicing Group Name, Alias and Location, ABA/CHIPS/DDA # and Name, Beneficiary Account and Type, Amount Matched, Amount Not Yet Matched, and Payment Reference Data.
Cashflows (other than transfer fees) for participation transfer buys cannot be created until the third party is assigned (since the cashflows are between the host bank buyer and the third party (the original seller of the circle).
If remittance instructions for a cashflow are IMT and cashflows have been released and the Circle is sub sequentially cancelled, user will not receive the usual warning that transaction cannot be un-canceled, since a circle can never be un-canceled.
If Funding Decisions needs to be changed before Circle has closed, but IMT Cashflows have already been released, user must first cancel the released Cashflows before returning the Circle to 'Open'.
IMT cashflows, associated with a circle sell when the Host Bank has a zero position in the deal and is buying and selling on the same day, can be released, provided that the Servicing Group can be defaulting from any unclosed circle buys for the branch. Defaulting the servicing group allows the Circle Sell to be sent to Settlement Approval, after which the IMT cashflows can be released in the normal manner.
Beginning with Release 6.0.09.02 and forward, cashflows can be split for Circle transactions.
When changes are made to these transactions which would change the cashflows, the cashflows are deleted. A warning message is displayed and the transactions are re-derived without the splits and unfrozen the next time they are accessed.
For more information on Split Cashflows, please see the Cashflows Edit and Validation Rules document.

items.label: text
items.orig: Example: The scenario is that there is not sufficient position in the affected portfolio positions to cover the sell. In that case, the portfolio allocations will be created as short (to the extent necessary). For example, the circle sell is allocated 1,000.00 to portfolio 1/expense code 1 and 600.00 to portfolio 2/expense code 2. The lender is changed from Host Bank A to Host Bank B. For Host Bank B, the trade date net position in portfolio 1/expense code 1 is 800.00, and the trade date net position in portfolio 2/expense code 2 is 1,000.00. Therefore, the new allocations will be 800.00 long and 200.00 short in portfolio 1/expense code 1; 600.00 long in portfolio 2/expense code 2.

items.text: Change to Buyback

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 1. Option is available to closed external Participation Buys only (not including swaps or participation transfer buys), and changes the closed Participation Buy to a closed Participation Buyback. Option is intended to correct those situations where the initial circle was erroneously set up as a Buy, when it must have been a Buyback. (A Participation Sell and Participation Buy for the same deal and lender are treated as two separate transactions, with money flowing in both directions. The money for a Participation Sell and a Buyback for the same deal and lender is netted, and if not an exact wash, flows in only one direction)

items.label: text
items.orig: Provided that the Delayed Compensation Applies indicator is set to Yes (checked), once the Delayed Compensation Start Date is reached, the nightly batch will calculate and post entries for Delayed Compensation. The batch will continue to calculate, accrue and post Delayed Compensation entries each night up to the Expected Close Date of the Circle. Once the Expected Close Date has been reached, provided the circle has not been Approved for Settlement, the batch will continue to calculate and post the Delayed Compensation amounts but will not accrue any more days (this also will not include the Expected Close Date as this is the date the circle is theoretically supposed to close and therefore no compensation is due).

items.orig: Beginning in 6.0.10.05, the Delayed Compensation module supports recent Loan Market Association (LMA) regulations pertaining to par trades. Loan IQ's delayed compensation calculations for all LMA par trades done on or after January 25, 2010 are identical to those for distressed trades, provided the following three conditions are met:
items.text: Beginning in 6.0.10.05, the Delayed Compensation module supports recent Loan Market Association (LMA) regulations pertaining to par trades. Loan IQ's delayed compensation calculations for all LMA par trades done on or after January 25, 2010 are identical to those for distressed trades, provided the following three conditions are met:

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 1. On the Details tab of the Circle notebook, Distressed is not selected. This defines the trade as a par trade.
items.text: On the Details tab of the Circle notebook, Distressed is not selected. This defines the trade as a par trade.

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 2. On the Codes tab of the Circle notebook, a Trade Settlement Standard of LMA is selected. In the Trade Settlement Number of Days table, Par Settlement Number of Days is defined.
items.text: On the Codes tab of the Circle notebook, a Trade Settlement Standard of LMA is selected. In the Trade Settlement Number of Days table, Par Settlement Number of Days is defined.

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 3. The new system parameter, DCDLP (Delayed Compensation Cut-off Date for LMA Par) is set. It defines the cut-off date. Any trade done before the cut-off date (its default value is January 25, 2010) is subject to the previous system behavior for calculation of delayed compensation of par trades. Any trade done on or after the cut-off date is subject to the new behavior, and this functionality only applies to trades done on or after the cut-off date.

items.orig: Option is enabled for all Participations, Assignments, Broker Transactions and Internal Trades (that is, for all distribution circles except distribution primaries) and for Outside Assignments in Deals where the Host Bank is Agent . Option is applicable to both Buys and Sells, and event fees may be entered for a circle at any time prior to circle close. Once the circle is closed, event fees (of any type) cannot be entered or updated. Circle Event Fees may be charged in the currency other than the deal currency. Cashflows for each of the fees will be in the currency of the fee.

This functionality is controlled by the system parameter UDEHA (Use Deal Expense Code for Host Assignment Recordation Fee Income) . When the Override Circle Closing Fees license is enabled, the Applies to Income or Applies to Expense indicators specify whether the Override Expense Code applies to either Income, or Expense, or both. The system parameter DAOEA (Default Assignment Recordation Fee Override Expense Applicability) determines the default values of the Assignment Recordation Fee Override Expense Code indicators for Income and for Expense, if the UDEHA system parameter is enabled. This is applicable only when an expense code is added where none previously existed. If an Override Expense Code exists, at least one of the indicators must be checked. For existing circles where an assignment recordation fee override expense code exists, both the Applies to Income and Applies to Expense indicators are enabled by default, to reflect the existing functionality.

items.orig: Loan IQ now allows zero value circles with event fees to be sent for settlement approval and generates cashflows/GL entries for the trades. table_cells.text: Defaults to the deal currency but may be modified to any active currency specified in the Currency Table.

If templated at the deal level, the appropriate Assignment Recordation Fee amount and its currency (for Inside or Outside the Bank Group) will flow down to the circle from Deal pricing when the circle amount is first entered. Unless Host Bank Seller is the Admin Agent, the entire fee also flows to Paid by Seller, and Paid by Buyer is set to zero. All amounts (Total Amount of the Fee, Paid by Seller and Paid by Buyer) may be overridden subject to following rules, but the sum of Paid By Buyer, Paid By Seller and Amount Waived must equal the Total Fee Amount. Except for pooled circles, assignment recordation

fees cannot be split between the buyer and seller, when either one is a Host Bank who is also the Admin Agent for the deal. Pooled circles can still be split between 'Paid By Buyer' and 'Paid by Seller,' even when one of the pool members is the Host Bank Admin Agent, since other pool members may be splitting the fee. (In determining whether the Host Bank Buyer or Seller is the Admin Agent, only the Legal Entity Names are checked. The branch of the Admin Agent is not checked against the Branch of

Since Host Bank Admin Agent does not pay any portion of the assignment recordation fee, error message is issued if user attempts to enter 'Paid by Buyer' (for Host Bank Buyer) or 'Paid by Seller' (for Host Bank Seller) when Host Bank is Admin Agent.

Note: 'Inside the Bank Group' means that the Buyer of the assignment currently has a non-zero (closed) contractual share of the deal (in any servicing group); otherwise, buyer is considered to be 'Outside the Bank Group'. (For broker assignment buys, the buyer will seem to be the booking bank, and the inside/outside bank group check will be based on its contractual share. This approach is not correct and will be corrected when broker transactions are redesigned in a future release).
Notes: If user manually enters a fee amount before circle amount is initially entered, subsequent flow down from deal will not occur.

table_cells.text: Host Bank Agented Deals: Host Bank Sells: When the Host Bank is both Agent and Seller and has the same branch, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (Unchecked) and be protected. Host Bank seller's portion, if any will always be waived. Cashflow is as follows: From the Non Host Bank Buyer to the Host Bank Agent/Seller. This will be reflected on the Funding Memo. When the Host Bank is both Agent and Seller, but the Agent and Seller are different entities and/or have a different branch, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked.) When the indicator is unchecked: Cashflow is as follows: From Non Host Buyer to Host Bank Seller as well as from Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent. This will be reflected on the Funding memo. When the indicator is checked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent as well as from Non Host Buyer to Host Bank Agent. Host Bank Buys: When the Host Bank is both Agent and Buyer and has the same branch, the 'Paid by Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked) and be protected. Host Bank Buyer's portion, if any, will always be waived. Cashflow is as follows: From Non Host Seller to Host Bank Buyer/Agent. This will be reflected on the Funding memo. When the Host Bank is both Agent and Buyer, but the Agent and Buyer are different entities and/or have a different branch, 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked), but can be changed. When the indicator is unchecked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Buyer to Non Host Bank Seller and To Host Bank Agent from Non Host Seller. This will be reflected on the Funding Memo. When the indicator is checked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Buyer to Host Bank Agent and from Non Host Seller to Host Bank Agent. This will NOT appear on the Funding Memo, as no cash has passed between the Buyer and the Seller. Outside Assignments: When an Outside Assignment is created for a Host Bank Agented Deal, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No,' but can be changed. Cashflows are as follows, and will NOT appear on the Funding Memo in either case: When the indicator is unchecked: From Non Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent. When the indicator is checked: From Non Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent and From Non Host Bank Buyer to Host bank Agent. table_cells.text: For Broker Transactions, the Broker is the booking bank and cannot be changed. For Host Bank Assignments and Participations, a Broker must be defined in order to save a non-zero Broker Fee Amount. If broker fee is zero, any broker assigned to the circle will be removed (after issuing a warning message). Any customer, regardless of Profile Type, may be named as Broker; however, at BTU, the customer receiving the Broker Fee must have a valid MCN. Note: When entering a broker, an error will be displayed if the broker is the circle buyer or seller or is the third party in a circle which requires a third party (i.e., a participation transfer). If an optional third party is entered, the broker may be the same as that optional third party. If a party to the circle is changed to be the same as a previously entered broker, the error will be picked up when attempting to approve the circle for settlement (or close the circle) or the next time a change is made and saved on the Event Fees screen.
Defaults to the deal currency but may be modified to any active currency specified in the Currency Table.

User enters broker fee amount (the amount host bank pays to a broker), which can be zero. Notes: If Broker Fee Amount is zero when 'OK' is pressed, the system will remove any broker assigned to the circle (except for broker transactions, where the broker is the booking bank), after displaying a working message. G/L entries for broker fees will default to the Expense Code of the Circle's Portfolio Allocations. If multiple Portfolio Buckets were involved, the system will use the first non-zero bucket in the first Facility Investment. For broker fees on internal assignments and participations, the branch and expense code depends on whether the cashflow is from the point of view of the buyer or seller. If from the point of view of the buyer, it will be the buyer's branch and expense code; otherwise, it will be the seller's. If portfolio allocations have not yet been done when G/L entries are projected, an error message will be displayed.

The fee can be owed to the buyer or the seller, depending on the current funding rate as of two days prior to settlement and the funding rate of the current outstanding loans. If the funding rate is higher, then the seller pays the buyer. If the funding rate is lower, then the buyer pays the seller. The Breakfunding Fee can be entered as either a positive or negative value. For a sell, a positive Breakfunding Fee indicates that the host seller pays the fee. If the Breakfunding Fee is negative, then the host seller receives the fee. For a buy, a positive Breakfunding Fee indicates that the buyer receives the fee. If the Breakfunding Fee is negative, then the host buyer pays the fee.

items.label: text

items.label: text
items.orig: Actual Settlement Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid when received: Default When 'Paid by Buyer' is selected. The Buyer is purchasing any unpaid interest prior to the Circle Close Date. Any cycles with unpaid Interest will appear on the Funding Decisions screen for a loan eligible for Funding Decisions. Interest Settlement Decisions must be made for the unpaid cycles when Principal Funding occurs. The default Interest Settlement amount is calculated based on the pro rata funding decision for the loan. For the current cycle, the period of interest calculated for the interest settlement is from the Cycle Start Date to, but not thru the Expected Close Date of the Circle. If 'Paid when received' is selected, the Buyer does not pay the Seller for the interest purchased until the borrower makes an interest payment. Therefore, there will be no cashflows or G/L entries when the circle closes, although the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustments are released for any interest cycle being purchased and an Interest Participation is created on the Cycle Shares screen in the loan notebook to account for the cashflow due to the seller or from the buyer for the interest purchased, to be settled when the interest payment is made by the borrower. When creating the Funding Memo, a message will be issued asking the user if they wish to include the Interest Decisions on the Funding Memo.

items.orig: If the entire portion of host bank commitment for a facility is sold and the trade is created and closed on CBD, and if the interest/fee settlement is selected as Paid by buyer at Circle Close , then a penny difference in interest proration issue may arise due to different rounding logic used by accruals (batch) and  circle  (online).  The  issue  occurs  when  the  system  calculates  interest  proration  amount  to  be greater than the actual interest accrued (by a penny), which leads to an error at the time of circle close - "Circle is selling more interest than exists in the current accrual share for the loan. Please do a cycle shares adjustment to move the required interest to the current Portfolio Position. "For such cases, the workaround is to do a lender share adjustment of a penny. Penny needs to be adjusted from a lender to host bank, which allows the trade to go ahead.

items.orig: Actual/Other Date - Paid by Agent: The user entered date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). When the circle is closed, an Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment is created and released for the period from the Accrual Changeover Date to the Circle Close Date. As no interest is being bought or sold, there will be no cashflows Circle Notebook. There will, however, be a G/L entry in the circle for Interest Income for the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment.
items.text: Actual/Other Date - Paid by Agent: The user entered date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). items.label: text
items.orig: Actual/Other Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid when received: Default when selecting 'Paid by Buyer'. The user entered Accrual Changeover Date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). The Buyer has the option to purchase any unpaid interest cycles prior to the Changeover Date. Those cycles will appear on the Funding Decisions screen under the respective loans available for Funding. For example, the circle is closes on June 15, but the Accrual Changeover Date is June 1. The Buyer's legal ownership of the interest begins on June 1, as they would have on the 15 if Actual/Other Date had not been selected. Loan IQ will create an Automatic Interest Accrual Share Adjustment for the period from the Accrual Changeover date to the Circle Close Date. Since the Buyer is legally entitled to this interest, there will be no cashflows since nothing is being purchased. There will, however, be a G/L entry in the circle for Interest Income for the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment. Interest Decisions must be made on any past due interest which falls prior to the Accrual Changeover Date. In this case, the Buyer does not pay the Seller for the interest purchased until the borrower makes an interest payment. Therefore, there will be no cashflows or G/L entries when the circle closes, although the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustments are released for any interest cycle being purchased. When creating the Funding Memo, the user is given the option of including the Interest Decisions.

items.orig: Flat: Only loans with a status of 'Non-Accrual' - can have an Interest Settlement Decision of Flat. If 'Flat' is selected has been selected, Interest Settlement Decisions cannot be made for accruing loans. Accruing loans will default to a settlement of 'Actual Settlement Date/Paid by Agent' and cannot be adjusted. A message to this affect will be issued when accessing the Funding Decisions Screen. In this case, the Seller is giving up all rights to the interest for all unpaid cycles for the portion of the loan the borrower is buying via the circle. The Buyer is assuming a share of all interest cycles based on their share of the principal and paying nothing to the seller. Those cycles will appear on the Funding Decisions Screen. The following text will appear on the Funding Memo for the interest being traded 'Flat': 'Interest has been traded Flat. Buyer will receive all interest if and when borrower pays.' Although there will be no cashflows for the interest which is being traded Flat, there will be G/L entries and an Automatic Accrual Shares Adjustment will be created for all unpaid cycles.

The calculation of the circle's share of a loan is sometimes referred to as "funding" the loan. When a short position is re-allocated, a 'Reallocation' transaction is created for the Portfolio Position on the Allocations Details ('Allocations for:') screen. To reallocate, the user may do one of several things. For example, if a short position has been created where there is actually sufficient Trade Date Available for allocation, simply eliminate the short position and create an actual allocation. items.label: text
items.orig: Allows user to flag which Host Bank Preferred Remittance Instruction(s) must be used as the Host Bank Corresponding Instruction. The toggle allows for 'Y' or 'N' selection, and the button will be disabled and indicator shown as 'N/A' for either Non-HB entities or non-applicable instructions. When looking for Host Bank corresponding instructions (to match to Incoming Money Transfer - Fed/CHIPS, IMT and Check) in preferred remittance instructions, the System first checks for a valid corresponding instruction with this Toggle H.B. Corresponding Indicator set to 'Y'. If there is only one such valid instruction, it will be used. If there are multiple such preferred remittance instructions, the System will select the first one. Otherwise, the System will look for the first preferred instruction which meets the criteria for use, and if none meet the criteria, then the System will look for the standard instruction; if no standard instruction exists that meets the criteria for use, then the System will look for the first one in the servicing group that meets the criteria for use. When looking for the preferred instruction for a cashflow with a host bank customer, if there is only one valid preferred instruction regardless of the setting of the indicator, the System will use that instruction. If there is more than one valid preferred instruction but there is only one with the indicator set to 'N', the System will use the preferred instruction with the indicator set to N . Otherwise, the System will look for the standard instruction. In order to be considered valid, the corresponding Host Bank instruction must meet the following criteria for use: same product, balance type and currency and the opposite direction (always "To" the Host Bank).

items.orig: Host Lenders
items.text: Host Lenders

items.label: text
items.orig: The Host Bank Ongoing Servicing Group will be set automatically whenever possible. When a circle is created, the host-servicing group will be set to the servicing group, if any, currently assigned to the branch of the logged on user (if the host location specified by the user is also the location of the default servicing group). If no servicing group has yet been assigned at the time portfolio allocations are entered, saving the portfolio allocations will cause the servicing group to be set to the servicing group, if any, currently assigned to the branch of the portfolio allocations. Again, this will be done only if the host location is also the location of the default-servicing group. If the host lender or its location is changed, any existing servicing group for that lender will, of course, be removed. As part of the lender/location change, the system will again attempt to set a default-servicing group for the host lender. Until the circle closes, the user is free to set the host ongoing servicing group to any servicing group assigned to the host lender's location (since the user may be aware that the branch servicing group assignment is going to change by the time the circle closes). However, at circle close, validation will ensure that the current host ongoing servicing group is valid for the branch of the circle. If it is not, an error message will be displayed - it will tell the user either the name and location of the servicing group that is valid for the circle or that there is no servicing group that is valid for the branch of the circle. The user will have to change the circle to the correct servicing group (possibly having to change the host lender location to the correct location first).

Participation Transfer Buy - Required Third Party is the Lender from whom we are buying the Participation Transfer. The Third Party lender need not already exist in the deal but must have a Lender Profile and a completed Lender Location. Host Bank cannot be named as the Third Party on a Participation Transfer Buy. 5. Outside Participation Transfer - The Third Party is the Lender from whom the Participation is being transferred, is filled in by the system and may not be changed 6. Participation Transfer Sell - The Third Party is set by the system from the Source Participation Agreement assigned to the circle (which denotes the original Lender on the Participation Sale). Cannot be changed by the user except by changing the source agreement. 7. Outside Assignment - The Third Party is set by system to the lender whose position is the source of the Outside Assignment.

All attributes specified for the original transaction (amounts, events, status changes, etc.) are applied to the mirror-image contra circle (offsetting transaction), and vice-versa, throughout the life of the transactions, with few exceptions. For example, sending one to approval causes the contra circle to be sent to approval, changing amounts in one changes the amounts in the other. Canceling or terminating one also cancels or terminates the other, etc. The only exceptions to this rule are that the two transactions are approved independently of one another, each one's "Affects Trading Position" indicator can be set independently and each one's closed status may be changed (to another closed status) independently of one another. Also, the sell cannot be reopened, since the offsetting Buy is not eligible for re-opening.

items.text: Definition and Purpose of Risk Books

items.label: text
items.orig: Risk books are collections of portfolio/expense codes. From a business standpoint, risk books are a business unit's risk position, e.g. par trading's risk book is the net of portfolio allocations from all the buys and sells that make up par trading's position or trading book.

items.label: text
items.orig: Risk books were defined and implemented in Loan IQ because certain trading groups did not want other groups, or users, to see their positions in certain deals. Before risk books were implemented in Loan IQ, users with access to a deal could see the positions held anywhere in the bank and all the details of all circles on a deal.

items.label: text

items.text: Risk Books on Circles

items.label: text
items.orig: All circles require a risk book when they are created. A circle can have only one risk book. Once a risk book is selected for a circle, the user can only choose portfolio/expense codes that are in that risk book.
items.text: All circles require a risk book when they are created. A circle can have only one risk book. Once a risk book is selected for a circle, the user can only choose portfolio/expense codes that are in that risk book.

items.label: text
items.orig: Circle portfolio allocations may only be made to portfolio/expense code combinations, which are assigned to the circle's risk book.
items.text: Circle portfolio allocations may only be made to portfolio/expense code combinations, which are assigned to the circle's risk book.

items.label: text
items.orig: However, after a circle has closed, the risk book on that circle can be changed for access to that circle, even though the existing portfolio allocations would not change. For example, a deal might be trading at par and so be in the par risk book, and then start trading distressed. Management wishes to switch the deal to the distressed traders, and so to their risk book. The distressed risk book could then be put on all previously executed circles -- which had been executed in the par risk book -- to allow the distressed trader access to participation positions in that risk book and to price information on those circles.

One risk book could be defined, with all valid portfolio/expense code combinations 'assigned' to that risk book. All users who input circles or marks would be assigned to that risk book. On circle input, if a user only has one risk book in the access list, the risk book is automatically assigned to the circle, without user input.

The new portfolio allocations are completed in the same portfolio/expense codes as the previous allocations. The auto portfolio allocations must only refer to the portfolio/expense codes used by current non-zero allocations. It never refers to dormant zero allocations and their associated portfolio/expense codes when determining which portfolio/expense code to auto allocate to.
Due to the trade amendments, if short allocations need to be done, Loan IQ does auto short allocations.
Note: This can happen, for example, if the host bank buyer is changed from one host bank A to host bank B. This could cause the trade date portfolio position for host bank A to become negative (which is normally an error that would prevent the lender share change from being completed). In this case, Loan IQ automatically re-allocates sells in host bank A's position from long to short.
Automatic portfolio allocation after a trade amendment involving a share change prior to close is provided. This includes the auto portfolio allocation to a facility which previously had zero allocation.
Note: The functionality mentioned above shall apply only if the circle currently has portfolio allocations.
Users are provided the ability to auto complete portfolio allocations in the case of risk book amendments on trades.
Note : Available in Release 7.5.1.3 HF13 and later, if any sub-allocated child circle is changed from assignment to participation or participation to assignment, the remaining child circles are not changed. In
addition, the cancelled parent trade is also not changed. Hence, the change in the share type affects only the circle that is changed.
After a trade amendment involving a lender share type/transaction type which changes assignable amount, if the user opts to do automatic portfolio allocations, then the following rules apply:
Loan IQ does the new portfolio allocations in the same portfolio/expense codes as the previous allocation
If there are multiple portfolio expense codes, the amount shall be allocated across the multiple portfolio expense codes(portfolio positions) based on the previous split across these portfolio expense codes(portfolio positions)
After a trade amendment involving a lender change, if the user opts to do automatic portfolio allocations, then the following rules apply:
When changing lender, on pressing OK on the change lender screen to change the host bank lender, if the new host bank is associated with more than one branch, the user shall be prompted to select the branch for the new portfolio allocations
When a lender is changed and all the portfolio codes for the previous portfolio allocations are also associated with the new branch on the Portfolio and Branch Association code table, Loan IQ shall do the automatic allocation as follows:
Loan IQ shall do the new portfolio allocations in the same portfolio/expense codes as the previous allocation
If there are multiple portfolio expense codes, the amount shall be allocated across the multiple portfolio expense codes(portfolio positions) based on the previous split across these portfolio expense codes(portfolio positions)
When a lender is changed and all the portfolio codes for the previous portfolio allocations are not associated with the new branch on the Portfolio and Branch Association code table, Loan IQ shall display an error that 'All the portfolio codes for the previous portfolio allocations are not associated with the new branch on the Portfolio and Branch Association code table and hence automatic portfolio allocations cannot be done.'
After a trade amendment involving a share change prior to close:
If a facility amount is being increased from zero to non-zero, Loan IQ generates a warning that the portfolio allocations would get auto completed to the active portfolio/expense code of the existing non zero facility(s) , regardless of whether any of the amounts for any of those existing non-zero facilities are being changed, assuming the circle has facility allocations across only one portfolio/expense code and provides ability for the user to say yes/no
If the user confirms, then Loan IQ does automatic portfolio allocations as noted above
If the user does not confirm, then Loan IQ does not do automatic portfolio allocations and generates an informational message that automatic portfolio allocations have not been completed
Examples assuming user confirms automatic portfolio allocations must be done:
A circle has been entered with 100k against Facility A in portfolio/expense code P1, and 0 against Facility B
If circle gets amended via share change prior to close to be 50k against Facility A, and 50k against Facility B
The increase of 50k to Facility B must get auto allocated to portfolio/expense code P1
One circle has been entered with 100k against Facility A in portfolio/expense code P1
Circle gets amended via share change prior to close to be 0k against Facility A, and 100k against Facility B
The increase of 100k to Facility B must get auto allocated to P1
If the circle has facility allocations across multiple portfolio/expense codes, Loan IQ generates an informational message that automatic portfolio allocations cannot be completed
Example assuming user confirms automatic portfolio allocations must be done:
One circle has been entered with 50k against Facility A in portfolio/expense code P1, 50k against Facility B in portfolio exp code P2 and 0 against Facility C
Circle gets amended via share change prior to close to be 25k against Facility A, and 25k against Facility B and 50k against Facility C
The client will never have one circle with facility allocations across many portfolio/expense codes. Hence in a situation like above, Loan IQ generates an informational message that automatic portfolio allocations cannot be done
For a circle sell, if the trade amendment causes a change which results in a short situation to itself, then Loan IQ automatically does short allocations to the extent necessary if the user has selected option to do an automatic portfolio allocation.
Example: The scenario is that there is not sufficient position in the affected portfolio positions to cover the sell. In that case, the portfolio allocations will be created as short (to the extent necessary). For example, the circle sell is allocated 1,000.00 to portfolio 1/expense code 1 and 600.00 to portfolio 2/expense code 2. The lender is changed from Host Bank A to Host Bank B. For Host Bank B, the trade date net position in portfolio 1/expense code 1 is 800.00, and the trade date net position in portfolio 2/expense code 2 is 1,000.00. Therefore, the new allocations will be 800.00 long and 200.00 short in portfolio 1/expense code 1; 600.00 long in portfolio 2/expense code 2.
Note: The user doing the trade amendment needs to have update access to Circle > Trade Date Short in order for the circle sell to be automatically shorted.

Option is available only after circle close to correct just the Circled Amount, or to correct just the Closing Amount. Changes are made for 'documentation purposes only,' primarily so that the circle will appear correctly on Lender Query. Changes applied to the circle do not affect the lender's position, which may be adjusted only via Facility's "Lender Position" Query. (Ability to change Circled Amount after Circle Close also extends to Internal Trades.)
User may pro-rate a new aggregate amount, or may enter amounts for selected facilities. Either the "New Aggregate Amount" or "New Percent of Global" can be entered and the system calculates the value not entered.
Pool and Portfolio allocations are not adjusted.
When "Change Share After Close" is selected for a Pooled Sale, the edit validations that govern closing a pooled sale will be reapplied. A warning will be issued if "Change Share After Close" is selected for a Swap or Buyback transaction. If a lender has no investment in a facility at circle close, "change share" may not be used to give that lender a closing amount in that facility, although the "circled" or current facility investment amounts may be changed.

Changes Circled Amount effective as of the displayed Circled/Legal Trade Date. This is never the default selection, and does not alter either the closing or current (allocated) amounts.
Changes only the Current Amount. Not allowed on closed participation Buyback or Sellback. If no increase/decrease has occurred, effective date defaults to current date , but can be overridden to another date greater than the closing date and not greater than current date. If increase/decrease has occurred, effective date defaults to date of last Commitment Increase or Decrease , but can be overridden to another date not less than last Increase/Decrease date and not greater than current date. The corrected closing amount of any or all facility investments in a closed circle may now be set to zero.
Option 2 is the default selection.
Note: When reducing a primary's share of a facility investment to zero, the facility investment will be deleted from the database if:
The facility investment has no portfolio allocations, or its portfolio allocations are allowed to be deleted from the database.
A facility whose facility investments have all been deleted from the database can be subsequently deleted itself.
Change to New Lender/Location provides the choice of changing the circle's Buyer, Seller (or Outside Assignor for Outside Assignments) or Third Party Lender and/or Location.
The rules are:
Pool members and Host Bank Lenders may not be changed after circle close, although their locations may be changed.
Change Lender/Location - With the Validation Host Bank and Risk Book Selection at Circle Level enhancement, available as a patch in Release 6.0.09.08, Loan IQ limits the available Host Banks in the Lender list to the Host Bank associated with the Deal branch in an existing Circle. Loan IQ defaults the Host Bank Lender to the Host Bank Lender associated with the Branch of the Deal. For more information, please see the Circle, Additional Functionality, Validate Host Bank and Risk Book Selection at Circle Level enhancement in Online Help.
Selecting this option will bring up the Delayed Compensation window, provided the client is licensed for the functionality. Only Users with Update Access under Application Functions in User Profile will be able to modify Delayed Compensation Data. Users with Inquiry Only and Access Denied will be able to view the Delayed Compensation window.
Whether or not a circle will accrue Delayed Compensation depends on two factors:
Provided that the Delayed Compensation Applies indicator is set to Yes (checked), once the Delayed Compensation Start Date is reached, the nightly batch will calculate and post entries for Delayed Compensation. The batch will continue to calculate, accrue and post Delayed Compensation entries each night up to the Expected Close Date of the Circle. Once the Expected Close Date has been reached, provided the circle has not been Approved for Settlement, the batch will continue to calculate and post the Delayed Compensation amounts but will not accrue any more days (this also will not include the Expected Close Date as this is the date the circle is theoretically supposed to close and therefore no compensation is due).
The appearance of the Delayed Compensation window, Cost of Carry Rates, will depend on whether or not the Trade is Par or Distressed, which is determined by the setting of the Distressed indicator on the Detail tab of the Circle Notebook.
Note: As per the Payment in Kind (PIK) Interest enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05, the following separately licensed functionality applies:
If the facility is eligible for PIK and PIK Interest rules have been defined, circles with the facility use the PIK functions for Non-Cash Interest Accrual and not the Delayed Compensation functions.
Delayed Compensation only applies to the Cash Portion of the Interest Accrual. The PIK Portion of the Interest Accrual is not subject to Delayed Compensation.
In the case of distressed trades settled late, the buyer must still pay the seller the cost of carry. No interest income is paid to the buyer since the trade is distressed.
Beginning in 6.0.10.05, the Delayed Compensation module supports recent Loan Market Association (LMA) regulations pertaining to par trades. Loan IQ's delayed compensation calculations for all LMA par trades done on or after January 25, 2010 are identical to those for distressed trades, provided the following three conditions are met:
All Delayed Compensation window functionality that exists for distressed trades applies to LMA par trades (i.e., trades conforming to the conditions outlined above). For example, Cost of Carry is displayed on the Delayed Compensation window for LMA par trades. Other distressed trade functionality that applies to LMA par trades includes:
Accessing the Delayed Compensation Additional Amount window for Cost of Carry from the Delayed Compensation window
Calculating Accrued Interest & Fees as they are calculated for distressed trades
Controlling whether or not to Settle Unpaid Interest/Fees
The ability to drill down online items on the Delayed Compensation window to view Amount Paid To Date
As per the enhanced Delayed Compensation functionality available in Release 7.2.4 and patched to Release 6.0.12.02, the delayed compensation calculations for par and near par secondary loan trades have been modified to comply with new LSTA regulations pertaining to par trades. Loan IQ's delayed compensation calculations for all LSTA par trades done on or after June 29, 2012 are identical to those for distressed trades, provided the following three conditions are met:
All Delayed Compensation window functionality that exists for distressed trades applies to LSTA par trades, including:
Note : The Outstanding Ongoing Fee is not taken into consideration when Delayed Compensation Fee is calculated.

If the parent circle counterparty is outside the bank group and the assignment recordation fee outside bank group is not templated at the deal level, Loan IQ copies the entire fee to the first child.

If the fee is prorated, Loan IQ populates Paid by Seller for the child trade based on a prorated basis using the value populated in the parent trade.
If the fee is not prorated, Loan IQ populates the Paid by Buyer and Paid By Seller values as is from the parent trade to the first child.
Loan IQ populates Waived based on the same business rules applicable to the parent trade.

Note: As per the Enhance Zero Value Trades enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05 (Patch also for 08.02), the following functionality applies:
Loan IQ now allows zero value circles with event fees to be sent for settlement approval and generates cashflows/GL entries for the trades. Where the trade was originally allocated over multiple portfolios, the final GL posting for the event fee cashflows are pro-rated across the multiple portfolio/expense codes based on the allocation. Although the portfolio allocations are reduced to zero, Loan IQ still pro rates the event fee cashflows postings over the multiple portfolio/expense codes when closing a zero value trade.
In pro rating event fees on zero value trades that have had portfolio allocations previously done, Loan IQ looks at the timestamps of the latest commitment decrease (the one that brought the trade to zero) and takes the pro rata of the portfolio allocations from that particular commitment decrease.
For zero value trades that have not had previous portfolio allocations done, in pro rating event fees prior to the trade amount being brought to zero, Loan IQ prompts users to manually select the portfolio/expense codes across which to pro rate any event fees that may have been added to the circle and need to be settled. The selection of portfolio expense codes is based on the available portfolio/expense codes for the Risk Book of the circle.
