Assignment Recordation Fee: Applicable to all Broker and Host Bank Assignments including Internal Assignments. Applicable to Outside Assignments when Host Bank is Agent.
Broker Fee: Applicable to all Broker Transactions and to all Host Bank Assignments and Participations including Internal Circles.
Available in Release 6.0.12.11, the following separately licensed Cost of Carry Multi Currency Loan Calculation functionality applies:
Purchase Price computation during Cost of Carry calculation is modified only for Trades with multicurrency facility/facilities with delayed compensation as follows. Loan IQ calculates the Purchase Price for Cost of Carry calculations on a currency by currency basis, based on the individual loan currencies, as well as the Facility currency, as defined below:
Actual Settlement Amount Due from Buyer to Seller (excluding Delayed Compensation)
[Buyer's Share of the Funded Amount in Loan Currency @ Delayed Compensation Start Date] * [Buy/Sell Price]
Minus
[Buyer's Share of Undrawn Amount in Loan Currency** @ Delayed Compensation Start Date] * [100Buy/Sell Price]
[Buyer's Share of Commitment Reductions in Loan Currency++ on or after Trade Date but on or before Settlement Date] * [100-Buy/Sell Price]
[Non-recurring Fees in Loan Currency received by the Seller on or before the Settlement Date to which the Buyer is Entitled]
*Note : if this amount comes to a negative sum, the absolute value is due from Seller to Buyer
This amount is calculated for each applicable loan currency during multicurrency facility trades for Purchase Price calculation during cost of carry computation.
This calculation is same as followed in current circle funding memo in Delayed compensation applicable trades.
** Undrawn amount discount calculation in Loan Currency is only applicable when Facility and Outstanding are in the same currency. In other scenarios this amount is zero. The undrawn amount is always stated in the Facility Currency. Loan IQ calculates the undrawn amount piece of the Purchase Price as it currently does .
If the commitment reduction is due to a scheduled or unscheduled principal payment on or after the Circle Trade Date and on or before the Circle Close Date, then the benefit of commitment reduction due to principal payment is considered in the calculation of the purchase price.
For example in a fully funded term facility, a principal payment on Term Loan reduces its balance as well as causing the commitment reduction.
++ A Commitment Reduction is actually done in the Currency of the Facility. In the scenario where the Commitment Reduction is the result of a Loan Principal Payment with Auto-Reduce indicator checked, Loan IQ is able to determine the amount of the Commitment Reduction in the Loan Currency and that is used to calculate the Purchase Price balance for the Cost of Carry calculation in that Loan Currency. However, if the Commitment Reduction is done manually via the Facility Increase/Decrease Schedule, Loan IQ does not have a link to the actual Principal Payment and determines the amount of the Commitment Reduction in the Facility Currency and that will be used to calculate the Purchase Price balance for the Cost of Carry calculation in that Facility Currency.
If the fee payment is received on or after the Circle Trade Date and on or before the Actual Settlement Date (i.e. Circle Close Date), then the benefit of fee payment is considered in the calculation of the purchase price.
Here Non-recurring fees refers to only 'One time post trade date fee payment' fee which is not recurring in nature. In the event fees window 'Assignment recordation fee' is not included in the non-recurring fees.
In the event fees window above fee has a history button to capture the modifications to fee amount with dates.
History for above event fee modification is provided as based on the effective date of the modification (as entered by the user) and the modified amount delayed compensation will change. This amount is considered in non-recurring fee, which is included in the purchase price calculation.
In a deal, if a fee is paid in specific currency other than in the facility currency and there is no existing outstanding in that currency, then Delayed Compensation calculations are handled separately out of Loan IQ.
For example 'one time post trade date fee payment' amount may be entered on day one and then may be changed on day 5 and the purchase price calculation looks at the amount on the different dates.
In a deal, if a fee is paid in specific currency other than in the facility currency and there is no existing outstanding in that currency, then Delayed Compensation calculations are handled separately out of Loan IQ.
For any non-recurring fee that is not in the currency of any outstanding, Loan IQ does not include in the purchase price formula for cost of carry.
However, if the fee is in the currency of the facility (example: there is no outstanding in the facility currency) Loan IQ calculates and includes this fee in the purchase price formula for cost of carry.
Note: In the case of the unfunded discount where there are no loans in the facility currency, Loan IQ still calculates unfunded discount for the facility currency, using the formula (with the funded amount in currency as zero).

Displays all information needed for user to make a Funding Decision and, if applicable, allows user to request generation of the Funding Memo . Selection of "Funding" option is not applicable to Broker Transactions (Broker Participations and Assignments).
When selected in update mode, an error message is displayed if no outstandings exist for any facility in which the circle has a share. When selected in Inquiry mode, an 'empty' funding decision screen will be displayed under these circumstances. Funding Query is not applicable to circles that are never funded (for example, Outside Assignments in a deal for which the agent is not a Host Bank, Broker Transactions, Intraday Loans, Bankers Acceptances and Discount Loans).
Also, when selected in update mode, a warning is issued if no closing or ongoing Servicing Group exists for the buyer/seller (our Counterparty), noting that a Funding Memo cannot be prepared without a Servicing Group. (The user may still want to look at the Funding and/or make a Funding Decision. A Funding Decision can be made and saved even if a Funding Memo cannot be prepared).
Prior to Circle Close, displays outstandings (loans, non-loans, SBLCs, including any pending transactions) that are expected to be active on or before this circle's expected close date. Loans are listed by facility , for all facilities in which this lender is investing. Facility Name, Alias, Status (active or pending), Pricing Option, Repricing Date, this circle's pro-rata share of the outstanding, a 'funding decision' and the Global Current Outstandings are displayed.
Note: Circles with an updated close date prior to the current business date will base their funding decisions on the current outstandings. Circles with an expected close date in the future will base their funding decisions on the outstandings projected to be active on that date. In both cases, the funding decisions will be based on the outstandings as affected by any pending transactions expected to be released by that date.
Note: Pending payments for the entire principal amount cause the circle to ignore the loan because it reads the loan as having a zero amount. Therefore the loan is not funded and the lender does not show up in lender shares of the loan, even though the circle trade date and close dates are later than the loan effective date.
The funding memo shows information for all facilities in the circle for which the circle has a non-zero amount, regardless of whether or not there are any outstandings under that facility. If there are no outstandings, the memo states: 'No Loans Expected to be Outstanding Under Facility as of [expected closing date of circle].'
In addition, for any facility with loans expected to be effective at circle close, a line is shown regardless of whether or not the lender is funding the particular loan [Any loans not being funded are of course, shown with a zero loan share].
Note : SBLC's and Non-Loans are included in funding decisions so that shares may be pro-rated correctly, but are excluded from the funding memo and cashflows at time of circle closure (since they are not funded).
Intraday Loans, Discounted Loans and Banker's Acceptances are excluded from both the funding decision and from the funding memo and cashflows.
Funding Decision Effective Date is set to the Effective Date of the governing transaction. For instance, if a circle is closed effective 12/31/95, then the effective date of the funding decision will also be 12/31/95.
Funding Decisions can be made, and Funding Memos can be created, even when portfolio allocations have not yet been created.
Note : In the past adding a new outstanding and releasing an outstanding transaction have notified circles with frozen funding decisions for the outstanding, set funding to needs review, and returned settlement approved circles to open. This will no longer be done. Instead, frozen funding decisions will be set to needs review, as described below:
New Outstanding - When a new outstanding (of a type which can have a funding decision) is created, a funding decisions (i.e., Outstanding Automatic Share Adjustment) frozen at zero will be created for any circle which is approved for settlement and has a share of the outstanding's facility. This decision will be set to needs review
Releasing Outstanding Transactions - When an outstanding transaction is released, any non-zero frozen funding decisions for the outstanding will be set to need review.
If any funding decisions are set to need review, the user will not be able to release the first cashflow. If any cashflows were released before decisions were set to needs review, subsequent cashflows may be released, but the user will get a warning message. Circles may not close while there are any cashflows needing reviews.
The circle funding decision screen indicates whether a funding decision needs review ('NR' in red in the first column) . The user may review a decision, leaving it as is, by using the Review button. If it is necessary to change the decision, the circle must be returned to open. If any cashflows have already been released, they will have to be cancelled in order to return the circle to open.
Note: If there is a change to the Circle (e.g. Change in amount or change in Servicing Group if the Funding Memo has not been sent yet) user will receive an error message that funding needs review due to Circle Changes. If one or more individual funding decisions are set to needs review (NR), message is received that one or more frozen funding decisions need review due to change to outstandings.
The ability to net payments - If a particular lender does not want the standard Funding Memo (created by netting payments), the 'Settle Gross/Settle Net' indicator setting in the Circle Notebook can be changed from 'Settle Net' (default) to 'Settle Gross,' and the alternate version of the Funding Memo will be prepared.
As per the separately licensed Trade Settlement with Pending Loan Transactions enhancement, available in Patch Release 6.0.08.08, the following functionality applies.
In case of Pending Outstandings whose Effective Date is less than or equal to the Expected Closing Date of the Circle and which appear in the 'Funding Decision' screen of the Circle notebook, Lender Share
Adjustments are automatically created upon closing the Circle, even though the Funding Decisions for such Pending Outstandings are set to 'zero'.
If there are Pending Outstandings appearing in the Funding Decision screen of the Circle notebook, whose Funding Decisions are set to zero, and the Pending Outstandings are released after the Funding Decisions are frozen but prior to closing the Circle, Loan IQ displays an appropriate error message to the user at the time of closing the Circle. The user must then return the Circle Back to Open status and change the Funding Decision for the Outstandings which were released after the Funding Decisions were frozen and then proceed to close the Circle.
Three 'funding decisions' are possible:
'0.00' - Indicates the loan is not being funded (Set by choosing "Don't Affect" button) .
'float' - Indicates the Funding Memo has not yet been prepared but when it is, this loan will be included as one of the loans being funded, on a pro-rata basis . Until preparation of the Funding Memo, the lender shares are 'floating' (that is, they are being adjusted constantly as changes occur, so that they will remain on a pro-rata basis). (Set by choosing "Float" button).
Decision Amount - Displaying an actual amount, rather than '0.00' or 'float', indicates either that the Funding Memo has already been prepared and this loan was included for the amount shown, or, if the Funding Memo has not yet been prepared, that this lender's loan shares have been 'frozen' and will be included in the Funding Memo, when prepared, at the amounts shown.
Interest Settlement Decisions for Interest Bought and Sold: This functionality is not available for Risk Participations. The default will be Actual Settlement Date/Paid By Agent and cannot be changed. It is not available for any type of Internal Circle, other than Internal Assignments and Participations.
Depending on the above option, the Funding Decisions Screen, Funding Memo and Cashflows will behave as follows:
Actual Settlement Date - Paid by Agent: The Buyer of the circle assumes their share of the interest as of the Circle Close Date. Unpaid Interest Cycles do not appear on the Funding Decisions Screen. There are no cashflows or G/L's in the Circle Notebook and nothing appears on the Funding Memo.
Actual Settlement Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid when received: Default When 'Paid by Buyer' is selected. The Buyer is purchasing any unpaid interest prior to the Circle Close Date. Any cycles with unpaid Interest will appear on the Funding Decisions screen for a loan eligible for Funding Decisions. Interest Settlement Decisions must be made for the unpaid cycles when Principal Funding occurs. The default Interest Settlement amount is calculated based on the pro rata funding decision for the loan. For the current cycle, the period of interest calculated for the interest settlement is from the Cycle Start Date to, but not thru the Expected Close Date of the Circle. If 'Paid when received' is selected, the Buyer does not pay the Seller for the interest purchased until the borrower makes an interest payment. Therefore, there will be no cashflows or G/L entries when the circle closes, although the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustments are released for any interest cycle being purchased and an Interest Participation is created on the Cycle Shares screen in the loan notebook to account for the cashflow due to the seller or from the buyer for the interest purchased, to be settled when the interest payment is made by the borrower. When creating the Funding Memo, a message will be issued asking the user if they wish to include the Interest Decisions on the Funding Memo.
Actual Settlement Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid at close: The Buyer is purchasing any past due interest prior to the Circle Close Date. Any cycles with unpaid Interest will appear on the Funding Decisions screen for a loan eligible for Funding Decisions. Interest Settlement Decisions must be made for any unpaid cycles when Principal Funding occurs. The default Interest Settlement amount is calculated based on the pro rata funding decision for the loan. For the current cycle, the period of interest calculated for the interest settlement is from the Cycle Start Date to, but not thru the Expected Close Date of the Circle. The Buyer pays the seller for the interest when the circle is closed. The cashflows and G/L entries will appear in the circle. An automatic Accrual Share Adjustment (similar to the Automatic Lender Share Adjustment created by the funding decision), is created and released in the loan notebook when the circle is closed, for every affected interest cycle. The Interest Decisions will appear on the Funding Memo.
Beginning with Release TBD and patched to Release 6.0.10.05 with the Add Net Yield Interest To Loan Interest Circle Notebook enhancement, the 'Net Yield Cycle Due' for Interest Cycles is calculated based on the Net Yield Rate of those Outstandings (Loans and Loan-Like Outstanding Types) for whom Servicing Fee is applicable. This applies on any Interest Cycle in the Funding Memo when the 'Int/Fee' is set to 'Paid By: Buyer' and 'Paid At Close' in the Circle transaction.
There are no changes to Cashflows and GL entries in the Outstanding, Interest Payment or Circle notebooks.

If the entire portion of host bank commitment for a facility is sold and the trade is created and closed on CBD, and if the interest/fee settlement is selected as Paid by buyer at Circle Close , then a penny difference in interest proration issue may arise due to different rounding logic used by accruals (batch) and  circle  (online).  The  issue  occurs  when  the  system  calculates  interest  proration  amount  to  be greater than the actual interest accrued (by a penny), which leads to an error at the time of circle close - "Circle is selling more interest than exists in the current accrual share for the loan. Please do a cycle shares adjustment to move the required interest to the current Portfolio Position. "For such cases, the workaround is to do a lender share adjustment of a penny. Penny needs to be adjusted from a lender to host bank, which allows the trade to go ahead.
Actual/Other Date - Paid by Agent: The user entered date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). When the circle is closed, an Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment is created and released for the period from the Accrual Changeover Date to the Circle Close Date. As no interest is being bought or sold, there will be no cashflows Circle Notebook. There will, however, be a G/L entry in the circle for Interest Income for the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment.
Actual/Other Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid when received: Default when selecting 'Paid by Buyer'. The user entered Accrual Changeover Date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). The Buyer has the option to purchase any unpaid interest cycles prior to the Changeover Date. Those cycles will appear on the Funding Decisions screen under the respective loans available for Funding. For example, the circle is closes on June 15, but the Accrual Changeover Date is June 1. The Buyer's legal ownership of the interest begins on June 1, as they would have on the 15 if Actual/Other Date had not been selected. Loan IQ will create an Automatic Interest Accrual Share Adjustment for the period from the Accrual Changeover date to the Circle Close Date. Since the Buyer is legally entitled to this interest, there will be no cashflows since nothing is being purchased. There will, however, be a G/L entry in the circle for Interest Income for the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment. Interest Decisions must be made on any past due interest which falls prior to the Accrual Changeover Date. In this case, the Buyer does not pay the Seller for the interest purchased until the borrower makes an interest payment. Therefore, there will be no cashflows or G/L entries when the circle closes, although the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustments are released for any interest cycle being purchased. When creating the Funding Memo, the user is given the option of including the Interest Decisions.
Actual/Other Date - Paid by Buyer/Paid at close: The user entered Accrual Changeover Date will determine when the Buyer assumes their legitimate share of the interest accruals (as opposed to the Circle Close Date). The Buyer has the option to purchase any unpaid interest cycles prior to the Changeover Date. Those cycles will appear on the Funding Decisions screen under the respective loans available for Funding. For example, the circle is closes on June 15, but the Accrual Changeover Date is June 1. The Buyer's legal ownership of the interest begins on June 1, as they would have on the 15 if Actual/Other Date had not been selected. Loan IQ will create an Automatic Interest Accrual Share Adjustment for the period from June 1 to June 15. Since the Buyer is legally entitled to this interest, there will be no cashflows since nothing is being purchased. There will, however, be a G/L entry in the circle for Interest Income for the Automatic Accrual Share Adjustment. Interest Decisions must be made on the past due interest which falls prior to the Accrual Changeover Date of June 1. If the past due interest is settled as part of the circle close, cashflows and G/L entries will be created in the Circle Notebook for the Interest Decisions. The interest settlement decisions will appear on the Funding Memo.
Beginning with Release TBD and patched to Release 6.0.10.05 with the Add Net Yield Interest To Loan Interest Circle Notebook enhancement, the 'Net Yield Cycle Due' for Interest Cycles is calculated based on the Net Yield Rate of those Outstandings (Loans and Loan-Like Outstanding Types) for whom Servicing Fee is applicable. This applies on any Interest Cycle in the Funding Memo when the 'Int/Fee' is set to 'Paid By: Buyer' and 'Paid At Close' in the Circle transaction.
There are no changes to Cashflows and GL entries in the Outstanding, Interest Payment or Circle notebooks.
Flat: Only loans with a status of 'Non-Accrual' - can have an Interest Settlement Decision of Flat. If 'Flat' is selected has been selected, Interest Settlement Decisions cannot be made for accruing loans. Accruing loans will default to a settlement of 'Actual Settlement Date/Paid by Agent' and cannot be adjusted. A message to this affect will be issued when accessing the Funding Decisions Screen. In this case, the Seller is giving up all rights to the interest for all unpaid cycles for the portion of the loan the borrower is buying via the circle. The Buyer is assuming a share of all interest cycles based on their share of the principal and paying nothing to the seller. Those cycles will appear on the Funding Decisions Screen. The following text will appear on the Funding Memo for the interest being traded 'Flat': 'Interest has been traded Flat. Buyer will receive all interest if and when borrower pays.' Although there will be no cashflows for the interest which is being traded Flat, there will be G/L entries and an Automatic Accrual Shares Adjustment will be created for all unpaid cycles.
Loans with zero balances, but which still have unpaid interest will be displayed on the Funding Decisions screen in order for Interest Settlement Decisions to be made.
If a loan's principal Funding Decision is changed prior to close, the system will not regenerate the Interest Settlement Decisions based on the loan's new principal funded amount.
If any negative Accrual Cycles Exist for the loan (ex: an existing pre-payment on the current cycle), the Interest Settlement Decision cannot be made. User will receive error that an manual accrual share adjustment must be performed to correct the problem, or that Int Settlement options must be changed to 'Actual Settlement Date/Paid by Agent'. However, when an Interest Settlement Decision is tweaked for an individual cycle, the adjustment may be negative.
The Effective Dates of the Automatic Interest Accrual Adjustments cannot be greater than the Cycle End Date of the Cycle being adjusted.
If 'Actual Settlement Date', Interest Settlement Decisions will be allowed for both accruing and nonaccruing loans.
In the case of back valued trades, the current cycle will not be adjusted if the Circle Expected Close Date or the user entered 'Accrual Changeover Date' falls prior the Cycle start date of current cycle. The past cycle in which these dates falls must be adjusted.

Internal Assignments and Participations The Funding Decision is made via the Buy Side and applies to both the buy and the sell. Error is issued if user tries to fund (freeze) a funding decision for an Internal Circle before completing the portfolio allocations for both sides of the circle.
Note: As per the Payment in Kind (PIK) Interest enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05, the following separately licensed functionality applies:
The Funding Decision distinguishes the regular loans and the PIK Interest Loans, and presents both types of loans separately when the Funding Decision is being created.
Note: The Cost of Funds Spread on a Circle Buy Transaction can be modified by users with appropriate access.
Users must set the Index Rate for the matchfunded portion of the Circle Buy transaction before the Circle is closed. From the Set Cost of Funds window, an authorized user can override the value in the new Spread field, which is derived from the current Spread on the Funding Rates window. A non-authorized user may not override this default Spread value. If the Circle Buy transaction is past-dated, the Spread for the current date is used.
If the transaction is a Buy into an existing portfolio bucket, the Spread for the Buy is derived from the Spread defined on this bucket.
If the Buy results in the creation of a new portfolio bucket, the Spread applicable to Effective Date of the Circle Buy transaction is derived from the Funding Rates window. If the Circle Buy transaction is pastdated, the Spread for the current date is used.
Users cannot modify the Spread for the non-matchfunded portion of the transaction from the Circle notebook; however, an authorized user can modify the Spread for the non-matchfunded portion from the Outstanding notebook.
The Options Menu in the Funding Decision window offers the following choices:
Outstanding Notebook -Allows the user to easily enter the Outstanding Notebook of the particular outstanding that has been highlighted, and then exit back to Funding Decision Screen.
Validate Funding - Selecting this item will validate funding as if the circle were closing immediately. If there are any unsaved changes when this item is selected, the user will be informed, and the changes will be saved if the user chooses to continue. All error and warning messages are accumulated and displayed in one list at the end of the validation process with errors first and then warnings . This list is not modal to the funding decision screen and can remain open while the user makes any corrections to the funding decisions. 'Print' button is also available for hard copy listing of error and warning messages. If the circle is closed, Validate Funding option will not be available.
Generate TSI XML File - This command will only be available for licensed users of the TSI API functionality. These users can select this command to create a single XML file containing Trade Confirmation, Funding Memo, and Credit Agreement information for uploading to the Trade Settlement Inc. (TSI) system, facilitating the Secondary Loan Trading settlement process. This command is also available from the Options Menu of the Circle Notebook. For more information, licensed users may refer to the TSI API Guide on the Loan IQ Support Site. Non-licensed users
interested in learning more about this functionality must contact their Loan IQ Account Manager for more information.
The-Funding Memo Menu on the Funding Decision Screen offers the following choices:
CreateAllows the User to Create a Funding Memo. Funding Memos are created from a Default template which may be customized for specific branches. For more information regarding creating customized Funding Memo templates, refer to the Notice Templates Edit Val.
ViewAllows the User to View a Funding Memo which has already been created.
Funding Memos are required to inform lenders of the information they will need both to fund and to book loans for their Assignments and Participations. The Funding Amount is remitted by the lender to the Host Bank on a sell and is remitted by the Host Bank to the lender on a buy. Funding Memos are created to show a new lender his share of the current outstandings under each facility being purchased.
In order to create a Funding Memo for a circle, following validations must be passed:
The Funding Memo shows information for all facilities in the circle for which the circle has a non-zero amount, regardless of whether there are any loans outstanding under the facility. If there are no loans outstanding under that facility, the memo will state: 'No Loans Expected to be Outstanding Under Facility as of (expected closing date of the circle)'.
In addition, for any facility with loans expected to be effective at circle close, a line will be shown regardless of whether the lender is funding the particular loan. (Any loans not being funding will, of course, be shown with a loan share of zero. Previously, loans, which were not being funded, did not appear). Printing the Funding Memo saves it to the database.
Note: As per the Payment in Kind (PIK) Interest enhancement available in Release 6.0.08.05, the following separately licensed functionality applies:
The funding memo shows the amount of the original commitment that was sold on trade date, plus the corresponding amount of the commitment increase that was capitalized from trade date to settlement date. Commitment Bought or Sold Less PIK only displays a price. The Commitment Bought or Sold Less PIK represents the original commitment in the trade as amended by facility commitment decreases and share changes. The commitment increases are the proportion of any facility commitment increases due to PIK interest capitalization due that were allocated to the trade.
Funding memos for Assignment Buys include accrued interest and fees when the buyer pays interest and fee settlement at close, however the cashflows never include accrued interest and fees. User selects "Create' in the Funding Memo menu option to actually prepare the Funding Memo, after all loans to be funded have been chosen, and the lender loan share amounts have been calculated for each.
When the circle actually closes, the "potential" funding becomes real, and the lender actually assumes a share of the current outstandings of the active loans.
If user selects 'Don't Affect' for every loan that is expected to be active on a Circle's Expected Close Date, no warnings will be issued at Circle Close regarding funding, and no Funding Memo will be created.
Canceling a pending circle that has automatic share adjustments pending (representing the frozen funding decisions) also causes the pending adjustments to be deleted.
Calculation of Funding Amount Funding memo includes the Global Loan Amount as well as this lender's share of the loan, both in the currency of the loan if different from Deal Currency. The calculation of the circle's share of a loan is sometimes referred to as "funding" the loan. Circles that are not closed will automatically "fund" when a circle amount is entered, "refund" when the circle amount, Servicing Group, Lender Share Type or Lender Name is changed , and will have their funding amount automatically deleted when the circle is cancelled. On closing a circle, if the user has not specifically indicated whether or not the circle must be funded, a warning message will indicate that if the user continues, the circle will be considered funded (based on default funding).
All-In Rate - The All-In Rate shown on the Funding Memo for a particular loan is the Lender's Rate. If "Skim Pricing" pertains, it reflects the Borrower's All-In Rate plus or minus any relevant skim.
Remittance Instructions: Funding Memo obtains its Remittance Instructions from the preferred remittance instructions assigned to the cashflows. If no preferred instructions exist, the user may assign remittance instructions to the cashflows directly. The cashflows are from the point of view of the host bank, either to or from the other party. The remittance instructions used for the funding memo are always the other party's instructions.
The Funding Memo for Internal Assignments and Participations also finds its remittance instructions using the cash flows. Only 'Intercompany' or Interco/DDA can be assigned as payment method for remittance instructions for internal circles.

Changes to a closed circle's amounts, Servicing Groups, Lender Share Types, or Lender Name on circles that require a funding decision no longer automatically affect related loans. If such changes are to be effective, they must be made from the "Lender Position" Query in Facility Notebook. An event is created only when the funding status of the circle changes . If the status is 'Funding' or 'Funding/Memo Sent,' making changes to the funding decision (except changing it to not funding anything) does not create another event because it does not change the funding status of the circle. Likewise, if the funding status is already 'Funding/Memo Sent,' sending another memo does not create another event since the circle's funding status has not changed.
The Lender Pricing Screen that appears when the 'Interest Pricing' option is selected is composed of a Facility Selection Box and an Interest display area. Only one type of Interest Pricing is possible: Skim pricing (with zero skim = full interest).
For 'Skim' Pricing, a copy of the borrower's pricing text is displayed, with the relevant skim prominently shown above the text list box (as a number of basis points )and a "Show Spreads for Skim Pricing" button allows the user to change to a text view showing the lender spreads. To close a circle with 'Skim' pricing, the Branch, Portfolio and Expense Code for booking the skim must be defined, and the Branch must be the same as the Branch in the portfolio allocations for that facility investment.
If zero skim is specified, ' Full Interest ' appears above the text list box and the 'Show Spreads for Skim Pricing' button is disabled.
The "Modify Pricing" button is applicable only if circle is "Pending,' "Approved" or "Closed,' and may be selected only by users who are authorized to update the circle's pricing in its present state. Two possibilities exist : "Modify Pricing Pre-Close" and "Modify Pricing Post-Close.'
Skims and Buy/Sell price may be changed at any time. However, when circle is in a post-pending status, changing Skims, Buy/Sell Price or Pricing Type will be for "documentation" purposes only, and no price change events will be generated. In order to actually modify interest skims, Buy/Sell Prices or Pricing Types after circle close, the Facility Lender Positions Query must be selected and then the facility price information can be modified (adjusted).
Note : Skims are not allowed unless Deal Agent has a Servicing Group.

Maturity and Expiry Dates and the Portfolio Allocations List Box showing the existing allocations for a selected facility . Branch, Portfolio/Expense Code, Expense Code Description, Portfolio Allocation Amount, Assignable Amount and the Expiry and Closing Date are shown for each allocation.

Also, if portfolio allocations already exist in a Non-In Syndication portfolio, the buy/sell price cannot be changed to a price other than par (unless circle is already closed, and the change is for 'documentation only').
Buys - All Circle Buys except Internal Trades can be allocated to multiple portfolio/expense code "buckets.' Internal Trade buys must be allocated to a single portfolio/expense code "bucket'.

Assignable Amount -The portfolio position "Assignable Amount" is the amount that is available for assignments. When portfolio allocations are done for circles, the assignable amount may or may not be impacted. Net is always impacted.
The Assignable Amount will be impacted by assignment buys and sells, participation sells and participation buybacks.
It will not be impacted by participation buys; sub participation sells and sub participation buybacks.
It will be optionally impacted by portfolio transfers, internal trades and portfolio adjustments (depending upon a user-entered "assignable amount").
Excess Net - the amount by which the net position in a portfolio bucket exceeds the amount allocated to the assignable position.
Major Rule: Regardless of circle type, the Assignable position can never become greater than the Net position. Therefore, on transfers, internal trades and adjustments, the assignable must be within a minimum/maximum range that reflects the excess net position (that is, how much the net is greater than the assignable). A "Net only" transfer or adjustment can be applied only to the excess net position.
Minimum Assignable Amount the minimum amount that MUST be allocated to the assignable so that the assignable amount of the portfolio bucket will not become greater than the net. Applicable only to internal trades and portfolio transfers.
Maximum Assignable Amount the largest amount that can be allocated from the assignable without the assignable becoming negative. Applicable only to internal trades and portfolio transfers.

The user has the option to allocate some or all of the position as 'Short', but may not exit the Allocations window until the sum of the Short Amount and the Allocate (long) Amount is less than or equal to the sell amount. When a short amount is allocated out from an amortizing portfolio whose WAC is not 100, a warning will be issued ('Warning: A short amount has been allocated for an amortizing portfolio. A Circle cannot be approved for settlement as long as a short position exists. To reallocate, the user may do one of several things. For example, if a short position has been created where there is actually sufficient Trade Date Available for allocation, simply eliminate the short position and create an actual allocation. If a short position has be created in a portfolio where no long position currently exists, the user can perform a circle buy into the portfolio, thereby creating a position from which to allocate a long position.

The following methodology is used for reversal transactions for Circles that have ever had a Short position (rules below do not apply to In Syndication portfolios since the WAC and Discount is always 0):
Any circle that has ever had a Short Position performs the reversal transaction using the Aggregated Discount Methodology:
Commitment - Discount
Commitment x 100 = Price
Please note that the internal price, i.e. the price stored in the database and the price at which all calculations are done is not multiplied by 100). The displayed Price is multiplied by 100 as indicated in the formula above.
Commitment equals the Aggregated Portfolio Allocations commitment balance impacted by the reversal transaction.
Trade = $10MM, which was originally allocated as a complete Short Position.
Current Allocation:
$9MM Long
$1MM Short
The Commitment amount used in the above formula is the $9MM Long.
Discount equals the negated Aggregated Trade Date Discount of all the portfolio allocations associated with the portfolio bucket for this circle.
The resulting Price is used in the Portfolio Allocation reversal transaction to adjust the appropriate amount of Discount that corresponds with the Commitment reversed.
If the Commitment reversed is only a partial amount of the Circle Amount, then a pro-rata share of the commitment reversal will be applied against the Price, resulting in a pro-rata share discount reversal.

Note: The following rules apply to adding and removing the underwriter role to primaries:
If the underwriter role is added to a primary, the underwriter indicator is set to true on all other primary circles in the deal for the same lender. Likewise, if the underwriter role is removed from a primary, the underwriter indicator is set to false on all other primary circles in the deal for the same lender. Also, canceling a primary will delete all its roles only if it is the only primary in the deal for that lender.
The underwriter indicator will default to false if there are no existing primaries in the deal for the specified lender or if that lender does not already have the underwriter role in the deal. If the lender already is an underwriter in the deal, the indicator will default to true. If the primary is created with the underwriter indicator set to true, the indicator on all other primaries in the deal for that lender will also be set to true (and the underwriter role will be added as a role in deal for that lender). If the primary is created with the indicator set to false, the indicator will be set to false on all other primaries in the deal for that lender, and if the underwriter role already exists for that lender in that deal, it will be removed.
Note: All Roles will be removed, including underwriter, if the Primary Lender in the Circle is changed. No roles are removed if only the location of the Primary Lender is changed.

Entry of a positive amount increases the current balance of the WIP item; entry of a negative amount decreases it. The current balance of the WIP item may not be decreased below zero.

For a gain in the deferred portfolio, benefit of commitment reduction results in deferred P/L; for a loss, it results in realized P/L.

As per the separately licensed Commitment Reductions & Trade Entry enhancement, available in Patch Release 6.0.08.08, the following functionality applies.
For a trade that is created today (current business date), when the trade is circled and portfolio allocations are done, Loan IQ checks if any Commitment decreases were released today (current business date), to determine if the trade amount and/or benefit of commitment reduction need to be calculated for the trade. If the effective date of the commitment reduction(s) equals the circled date of the Trade, Loan IQ automatically reduces the open trade amount by the pro-rata percentage of the commitment decrease(s) and if necessary calculates and captures the benefit of commitment reduction for the trade.
This functionality applies when the trade is circled and the portfolio allocations are done regardless of how the trade is created, online or via the Trade API.
This functionality is applied once the trade is circled and the portfolio allocations are completed. Any subsequent modifications to the portfolio allocations or the Trade Circled Date will not invoke this functionality.
This functionality only applies to Host Bank Buy and Host Bank Sell circle trades and is controlled by system parameter APCR - Apply Prior Commitment Reductions , overridable by branch of the deal that the trade is for.
In regard to internal circles, system parameter ICBCR - Internal Circle Benefit of Commitment Reduction Applies determines whether benefit of commitment reduction applies to internal circles (including internal assignments and participations and internal trades). The benefit of commitment reduction is calculated for internal circles only if ICBCR - Internal Circle Benefit of Commitment Reduction Applies is turned on.
Any subsequent changes to the trade circled date or the portfolio allocations will not invoke this functionality. This functionality is only performed the first time the trade is circled and the portfolio allocations are done.
This functionality only applies to trades that are entered today (current business date), and the trade is circled and portfolio allocations are done.
The facility commitment reductions which are applied to the trade are those where the Commitment reduction was released today (current business date), the Commitment reduction effective date is equal to the circled date of the trade, and the create timestamp of the commitment reduction released event is prior to the create timestamp of the trade.
If the above criteria are met, Loan IQ does a circle share change prior to close for each facility in the trade that has a non-zero share. This circle share change prior to close reduces the share of the facility based on the following formula:
Circle Amount (facility Share) * (Sum of all the facility commitment decreases for the facility/(current global facility commitment amount + the sum of all the facility commitment decreases for the facility)).
The Sum of all the facility commitment decreases for the facility refers to the total amount of all applicable facility commitment decreases as defined above.
This circle share change prior to close adjustment is written to the event tab of the circle notebook with a comment that states it was due to previous released commitment reductions.
If applicable, Loan IQ also creates a Benefit of Commitment reduction adjustment on the trade.
The Benefit of commitment reduction appears in the circle notebook (similar to the way the current manual adjustment to benefit of commitment reductions appear on the circle). The GL entries for the modification to the Benefit of Commitment Reductions are associated with the Circle. No new GL entries are created for the previously released commitment reduction transaction.
This modification to the benefit of commitment reduction is written to the event tab of the circle notebook with a comment that states it was due to previous released commitment reductions.

The Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Internal Circles enhancement is available in Release 6.0.08.08 (Patch) and Release 6.0.09.08.
The Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Internal Circles enhancement is an extension of the existing Benefit of Commitment Reduction functionality to Internal Buy/Sell Transactions. This enhancement allows a benefit of commitment reduction to internal circles, transfer between two Host Bank legal Entities, as well as Internal Trades, and Trades between two Portfolio Positions within the same legal Entity.
System parameter ICBCR ( Internal Circle Benefit of Commitment Reduction Applies ) controls whether benefit of commitment reduction is applicable for internal circles. This parameter defaults to N , meaning that benefit of commitment reduction does not apply. This parameter is overridable by the branch (of the Deal).
If only one circle has portfolio allocations, benefit of commitment reduction will not be applied to either circle. The benefit of commitment reduction internal notification, which is generated when circles do not have portfolio allocations, has been enhanced to include these circles.
If both sides of the circle do not have portfolio allocations, benefit of commitment reduction will not apply. This is consistent with current Loan IQ functionality which does not apply benefit of commitment reduction if portfolio allocations do not exist.
If benefit of commitment reduction is manually applied to an internal circle, Loan IQ will not automatically apply benefit of commitment reduction to the contra circle. You will have to manually apply benefit of commitment reduction to the contra circle or you will be unable to close the circles.
All rules regarding benefit of commitment reduction and when it applies pertain to Internal Circles.
The Benefit of Commitment Reduction to Internal Circles enhancement will not work with the following functionality:
Portfolio Position Multi-Currency Discount
Pay-In-Kind Interest Functionality
Settlement Date Short Portfolio Position Functionality

Intra-bank transactions (Internal Circles) are secondary Buys and Sells (participations and assignments) transacted between two customers who are both Host Bank Legal Entities.
Internal Trades are Buy/Sell transactions between two different Risk Books within the same Host Bank Legal Entity (Customer). The two Lender Locations may be the same, or may be different.
Internal Trades do not require contacts, Servicing Groups or a Pricing Comment. (Contacts and Servicing Group are optional, but Pricing Comment cannot be entered). The only pricing allowed on an internal trade is the Buy/Sell Price, which is required. The commission to be paid by the buyer (instead of or in addition to any P&L generated by the difference between the price at which the seller originally obtained what is being sold), if any, may be entered as a Transfer Fee.
All Portfolio Allocation pertaining to Internal Trades will be Portfolio Transfers. Only one portfolio "bucket" may be specified for the source, and only one portfolio "bucket" may be specified for the target, when the allocations are performed. In all other ways, internal trades are similar to Intra-Bank Transactions (Internal Buy/Sells between two different Host Bank Legal Entities (Customers).
The "Affects Trading Position" Indicator is applicable to Internal Trades, defaults to "No" in both the Buy and the Sell and either may be changed to "Yes" independently of the other. The "Buy" may affect the Trading Position and the Sell may not, or vice versa, similar to the independent settings in Intra-Bank Transactions.
No on-line notifications are prepared or sent for Internal Trades.

Risk books are collections of portfolio/expense codes. From a business standpoint, risk books are a business unit's risk position, e.g. par trading's risk book is the net of portfolio allocations from all the buys and sells that make up par trading's position or trading book.
Risk books were defined and implemented in Loan IQ because certain trading groups did not want other groups, or users, to see their positions in certain deals. Before risk books were implemented in Loan IQ, users with access to a deal could see the positions held anywhere in the bank and all the details of all circles on a deal.
With risk books in Loan IQ, every user is given access to only certain risk books and so can see positions only in those risk books. Some users may be given access to all risk books.
Note that, regardless of risk book access, users may only see positions in deals to which they have separate deal access.
A user's access to specific risk books is defined in user profile. User has access to any Risk Book included in user's 'Risk Book Access' List. For each risk book to which a user is given access, authority may additionally be granted to:
If a user is given access to a risk book, but not been granted specific authority to buy/sell or view prices, then the user can see all circles in the risk book but not drill down to the circle notebook.
View Price authority allows the user access to the circle notebook for each circle in that risk book. This allows viewing all buy/sell prices, trade dates, and portfolio position information (for example, Trade Date Net Position, Closed Position, skim, average cost, trader and approved marks, discounts, etc.)
If a user is granted buy/sell authority in a risk book, then that user will also have view price authority. He may however be granted view price authority in any particular risk book without being granted buy/sell authority.
In any risk book to which a user has access, that user may only see the deals to which he has access.
All users may see the public bank group view (i.e. all primary and assignment positions, including amounts and lenders, but no prices and no participation information) in all risk books for deals to which they have access.
A user may also be given View All access to risk books. This allows the user to see all information in all risk books (though he must be given separate buy/sell or enter trader mark authority for each risk book). View All also allows the user to see the net bank position on lender query and in the deal and facility notebook.
For users without View All, Lender Query will show all primary and assignment circles (open and closed), but will only show the participation circles in those risk books to which they have access. Further, prices will only be shown for those circles (primary, assignee, participation) in risk books to which the user has been given View Pricing authority.
Users without View All must not see the bank's true net position because they have not been given access to all risk books. Without View All, a user cannot see participation positions in those risk books to which he has not been given access. He must therefore not see the bank's net position because he could possibly derive participation information from knowing the gross and net positions in a deal.
Each circle on lender query will be identified with its risk book. "Secondary Available for Sale" has been changed in Release 2.2 to "Risk Book Available,' selection of which allows a user to see what is available for sale in those risk books to which the user has view access .
All circles require a risk book when they are created. A circle can have only one risk book. Once a risk book is selected for a circle, the user can only choose portfolio/expense codes that are in that risk book.
Circle portfolio allocations may only be made to portfolio/expense code combinations, which are assigned to the circle's risk book.
However, after a circle has closed, the risk book on that circle can be changed for access to that circle, even though the existing portfolio allocations would not change. For example, a deal might be trading at par and so be in the par risk book, and then start trading distressed. Management wishes to switch the deal to the distressed traders, and so to their risk book. The distressed risk book could then be put on all previously executed circles -- which had been executed in the par risk book -- to allow the distressed trader access to participation positions in that risk book and to price information on those circles.
If a bank does not need risk book security, it can give View All Risk Books (in user profile) to all users. However, note that users still need to be given buy/sell and trader mark authority independently, per risk book. One risk book could be defined, with all valid portfolio/expense code combinations 'assigned' to that risk book. All users who input circles or marks would be assigned to that risk book. On circle input, if a user only has one risk book in the access list, the risk book is automatically assigned to the circle, without user input.
One downside of defining only one risk book is that all traders would see, and have access to, all facility positions for input of trader marks.
Bank that is part of the syndicate and signs the credit agreement. Can influence the deal's structure and pricing. Has full voting rights on all aspects of credit agreement after close. Host bank origination primary requires portfolio allocations.
Bank that was brought into the deal by distribution personnel. Host bank cannot be a distribution primary.
Bank brought into deal via an assignment agreement. Assumes all of the rights and responsibilities of the primary. Has a direct relationship with the borrower. Requires portfolio allocations. In Loan IQ, Assignments are only made to/from the host bank. Assignments made between two non-hosts banks are created as Outside Assignments .
Bank brought into the deal via a participation agreement. Usually not known to borrower. Has limited voting rights. Requires portfolio allocations.

rules_table.Attribute: Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent
rules_table.Rules: The Assignment Recordation Fee functionality is available beginning with Release 6.0 and forward. Allows the User to direct the cashflow for the Assignment Recordation Fee to be paid by the Buyer directly to the Agent as an override to the normal functionality. Host Bank Agented Deals: Host Bank Sells: When the Host Bank is both Agent and Seller and has the same branch, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (Unchecked) and be protected. Host Bank seller's portion, if any will always be waived. Cashflow is as follows: From the Non Host Bank Buyer to the Host Bank Agent/Seller. This will be reflected on the Funding Memo. When the Host Bank is both Agent and Seller, but the Agent and Seller are different entities and/or have a different branch, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked.) When the indicator is unchecked: Cashflow is as follows: From Non Host Buyer to Host Bank Seller as well as from Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent. This will be reflected on the Funding memo. When the indicator is checked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent as well as from Non Host Buyer to Host Bank Agent. Host Bank Buys: When the Host Bank is both Agent and Buyer and has the same branch, the 'Paid by Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked) and be protected. Host Bank Buyer's portion, if any, will always be waived. Cashflow is as follows: From Non Host Seller to Host Bank Buyer/Agent. This will be reflected on the Funding memo. When the Host Bank is both Agent and Buyer, but the Agent and Buyer are different entities and/or have a different branch, 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' (unchecked), but can be changed. When the indicator is unchecked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Buyer to Non Host Bank Seller and To Host Bank Agent from Non Host Seller. This will be reflected on the Funding Memo. When the indicator is checked: Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Buyer to Host Bank Agent and from Non Host Seller to Host Bank Agent. This will NOT appear on the Funding Memo, as no cash has passed between the Buyer and the Seller. Outside Assignments: When an Outside Assignment is created for a Host Bank Agented Deal, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No,' but can be changed. Cashflows are as follows, and will NOT appear on the Funding Memo in either case: When the indicator is unchecked: From Non Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent. When the indicator is checked: From Non Host Bank Seller to Host Bank Agent and From Non Host Bank Buyer to Host bank Agent. Non Host Bank Agented Deals: When the Agent and the Buyer are the same Non the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to unchecked and be protected. Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Seller to Non Host Bank Buyer/Agent. The amount being remitted from the Seller to the Buyer will appear on the Funding Memo. When the Non Host Agent and the Non Host Buyer have different Location/Servicing Groups or are different customers, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' but can be changed. Cashflows are as follows: When the indicator is unchecked: From Non Host bank Buyer to Host Bank Seller and From Host Bank Seller to Non Host Bank Agent. The amount being remitted from the Buyer to the Seller will appear on the Funding Memo. When the indicator is checked: From Host Bank Seller to Non Host Bank Agent. This will not appear on the Funding Memo. Note: Beginning with Release 5.4.07.08 (Patch) , 6.0.08.02 (Patch) and Release 6.0.08.05 the following functionality applies: If recordation fees are being paid to the agent directly, the Funding Memo states whether the Buyer is paying the entire recording fee, the Seller is paying the entire recording fee, or the Buyer and Seller are splitting the recording fee and are paying separately to the Agent.

rules_table.Attribute: Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer
rules_table.Rules: Allows the User to direct the cashflow for the Assignment Recordation Fee to be paid by the Seller directly to the Buyer as an override to the normal functionality. Please note, the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer', is protected, until the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator is checked. Host Bank Agented Deals: Host Bank Buys or Sells: When the Host Bank is both Agent, and either the Buyer or Seller, the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' indicator will default to 'No' (Unchecked) and be protected. When the Host Bank is both Agent, and either the Buyer or Seller, but the Agent and Buyer or Seller are different entities and/or have a different branch, the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' indicator will default to 'No' (Unchecked) and be protected. Host Bank Agented Deals: Outside Assignments When an Outside Assignment is created for a Host Bank Agented Deal, the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' indicator will default to 'No,' and can only be changed when the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' is checked. If the Assignment Recordation Fee is to be Paid by the Seller, and the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' is checked, there will be a cashflow for the full amount of the fee from the Buyer to the Agent. This is due to the fact that 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' is only available when the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' is checked. Based on this, the Seller would send the fee to the Buyer, and the Buyer will remit the fee to the Agent. If the Assignment Recordation Fee is to be split between the Buyer and Seller, and the 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' is checked, there will be a cashflow for the full amount of the fee from the Buyer to the Agent. This is due to the fact that 'Paid By Seller Directly to Buyer' is only available when the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' is checked. Based on this, the Seller would send their portion to the fee to the Buyer, and the Buyer will remit the full amount of fee to the Agent. Host Bank Buyer to Host bank Agent. Non Host Bank Agented Deals: When the Agent and the Buyer are the same Non Host Bank Customer and the Host Bank is the Seller, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to unchecked and be protected. Cashflow is as follows: From Host Bank Seller to Non Host Bank Buyer/Agent. The amount being remitted from the Seller to the Buyer will appear on the Funding Memo. When the Non Host Agent and the Non Host Buyer have different Location/Servicing Groups or are different customers, the 'Paid By Buyer Directly to Agent' indicator will default to 'No' but can be changed. Cashflows are as follows: When the indicator is unchecked: From Non Host bank Buyer to Host Bank Seller and From Host Bank Seller to Non Host Bank Agent. The amount being remitted from the Buyer to the Seller will appear on the Funding Memo.

If the highlighted loan's Funding Decision is 'float,' the button 'Freeze' is available and depressing it calculates, displays and freezes the lender's pro-rata share of the selected loan. This means that the lender's loan share will not be adjusted to keep it on a pro-rata basis as subsequent changes occur. Conversely, if the highlighted loan's Funding Decision displays an actual amount, the button reads 'Float' and depressing it changes the funding decision back to 'Float.' Note: Once a decision is frozen, it is preserved even if the circle close date is prior to the loan's effective date. However, when the Automatic Share Adjustment is released at circle close, it is released as-of the latter of the Circle Close date and the loan's effective date. Note: If the funding decision is frozen, the projected and frozen outstanding columns on the Funding Memo will reflect the same amount unless a change has occurred to the principal, causing the projected outstanding amount to be different.

If the highlighted loan's Funding Decision displays an actual amount, the button 'Don't Affect,' is available and depressing it removes the loan from the group being funded and sets its funding amount to '0.00.' Conversely, if the highlighted loan's 'Funding Decision' is '0.00,' the button 'Affect Pro-Rata' is available and depressing it calculates and displays the lender's pro-rata share of the related loan. This amount will then either float (be adjusted to keep it on a pro-rata basis as subsequent changes occur) or be frozen, depending upon how the Float/Freeze button is set. Note: If the 'Float' or 'Don't Affect' button is clicked and the highlighted funding decision is returned to 'Float' or '00.00', the Interest Settlement Decisions must be returned to zero.

Third Parties are the source Lender for Outside Participation Transfers, Participation Transfer Sells and Participation Transfer Buys. Required for Participation Transfer Buys; set by system on Outside Assignments and Outside Participation Transfers; optional on all other types of circles. 4. items.text: The time zones of facilities affected by the circle are locked, as follows:

items.label: list_item
items.orig: 1. On circle create, no time zones are locked (since no lender share is specified) unless the circle is a buyback, sell back, participation transfer sell or outside participation transfer for which the full amount checkbox was checked. In that case, the time zones of facilities in which the circle has a lender share are locked by the circle create process.
items.text: On circle create, no time zones are locked (since no lender share is specified) unless the circle is a buyback, sell back, participation transfer sell or outside participation transfer for which the full amount checkbox was checked. items.label: list_item
items.orig: 2. On putting the circle notebook into update mode (or opening it in update mode), the time zones of facilities in which the circle has a lender share are locked by the circle notebook.

items.label: list_item

items.text: Since the circle amount may be changed directly in the circle notebook when first increasing it from zero, saving the circle locks (for the circle notebook) the time zones for facilities for which a lender share has been added.

items.label: list_item

On completion of the share change the time zones are unlocked for share change and relocked for the circle notebook, which also unlocks the time zone for any facilities, which no longer have a lender share.
